Open a pool and wrap it, as the README does (the caller closes the pool):

pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, url) // (ctx, string) (*pgxpool.Pool, error)
if err != nil { return err }
defer pool.Close()
db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool)) // New(pool, opts ...Option) momo.Driver

DSN: postgres://user:password@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=verify-full. Use sslmode=disable for local development only.

With database/sql: pgxdriver.FromConnConfig(cfg *pgx.ConnConfig, opts ...Option) (*sql.DB, momo.Driver) or pgxdriver.FromSQLDB(db *sql.DB). These have no Batch or COPY path.

Existing transactions: db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.SQLTx(sqlTx)) and db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.PgxTx(pgxTx)) run momo inside a transaction the caller began (Commit and Rollback return ErrAdoptedTx; the caller finishes it), and pgxdriver.UnwrapSQLTx(tx) or pgxdriver.UnwrapPgxTx(tx) give legacy code the *sql.Tx or pgx.Tx behind a *momo.Tx. Committing or rolling back the unwrapped handle of a momo-begun transaction is not allowed; momo still owns it. An adopted pgx.Tx keeps Batch (relation loading pipelines) and COPY; COPY is always binary, so vector columns need the pgvector codec on the caller's connection (ConfigureVectors on the pool, or your own AfterConnect). An adopted *sql.Tx has neither. PgxTx accepts the options of New; an exec mode that WithExecMode rejects makes every statement, batch and COPY on the adopted transaction return ErrUnsupported, as with New.

Vectors need the pgvector vector extension in the database. The generated migration emits CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "vector" when a model has a vector column (see vectors.md).

PgBouncer (transaction pooling): pgxdriver.New defaults to pgx.QueryExecModeExec (unnamed statements), and the CI PgBouncer tests open a pool and use New(pool) with that default, so no setting is needed. With FromConnConfig the exec mode is cfg.DefaultQueryExecMode, which pgx defaults to CacheStatement (not PgBouncer-safe), so set cfg.DefaultQueryExecMode = pgx.QueryExecModeExec before calling it; its opts have no effect.

docs.title: JSON operators and date and time expressions
docs.text: Feature API PostgreSQL SQLite MySQL / MariaDB JSON operators on types.JSON[T] jsonop.Text, jsonop.Path, jsonop.Contains, jsonop.HasKey yes jsonop.Text, jsonop.Path and jsonop.HasKey run on both SQLite drivers; a JSON boolean extracts as 1 or 0; jsonop.Contains is ErrUnsupported, since json_each cannot express the recursive @> rule SQL is golden-tested only; no integration test runs it against a MySQL or MariaDB server Date and time expressions timeop.Extract, timeop.AtTimeZone, timeop.Trunc, timeop.Now, timeop.CurrentTimestamp, timeop.IntervalOf, timeop.IntervalExpr, timeop.AddInterval, timeop.SubInterval yes every timeop.ExtractField, timeop.TruncUnit, interval and timeop.Now run on both SQLite drivers; month arithmetic overflows into the next month (Jan 31 plus a month is Mar 2 or 3, where PostgreSQL and MySQL clamp); timeop.Now is millisecond text; timeop.AtTimeZone is PostgreSQL only SQL is golden-tested only; no integration test runs it against a MySQL or MariaDB server; timeop.AtTimeZone is PostgreSQL only

docs.title: Core queries
docs.text: Feature PostgreSQL SQLite / MySQL API Insert one / many yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) Insert[T]: .Model(&m), .Models(ms), .Values, .ValuesRows, .Omit, .Exec Insert chunking over the bind limit yes, atomic (one transaction, or a savepoint inside a Tx); MaxParams 65535 SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet Models + Exec; WithMaxParams(n) lowers the limit; one row over the limit: ErrLimitExceeded Insert as one unnest statement yes: InsertQuery[T].Unnest() sends one array parameter per column, so the bind count does not grow with the rows and MaxParams / WithMaxParams do not apply (one statement, no chunking) ErrUnsupported on SQLite and MySQL Model / Models only (InsertQuery.Values, InsertQuery.ValuesRows and FromSelect give ErrValidation); needs the table schema in the generated metadata, or ErrValidation. Int, float, bool, string, time.Time and []byte columns bind as typed arrays ([]*T when a value is NULL); other element types (uuid, json, decimal, named enums) fall back to []any, which pgx may reject, so use plain Models for such a model. OnConflict, Upsert and Returning work as for Models; interceptors, BeforeInsert, field validators, automatic timestamps and id generators run as for Models. A FlagSensitive column's array is RedactedArg in QueryEvent.Args. Not the package-level FROM source momo.Unnest Select yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) Select[T]: Where, OrderBy, Limit, Offset, Distinct, All, One, First, Count, Exists Update, Delete yes; without Where they fail with ErrUnfilteredMutation unless .AllRows() SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) UpdateQuery[T].Set(...), Delete[T] UPDATE ... FROM, DELETE ... USING, WITH on DML, DML as a CTE body yes: UpdateQuery.From, DeleteQuery.Using, InsertQuery.With / InsertQuery.WithRecursive on InsertQuery, UpdateQuery and DeleteQuery, and an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE with Returning as a SelectQuery.With body SQLite: UPDATE ... FROM and WITH before any DML yes, DELETE ... USING and a data-modifying CTE body ErrUnsupported. MySQL and MariaDB: multi-table UPDATE t, src SET ... and DELETE t FROM t, src; WITH before UPDATE and DELETE on MySQL only (MariaDB ErrUnsupported, not verified); WITH before INSERT and a data-modifying CTE body ErrUnsupported From / Using take a table, momo.CTE or momo.FromSubquery; the soft-delete filter and interceptors do not apply to that source. With From or Using, Where must reference the target table or the statement is ErrUnfilteredMutation unless AllRows. A WITH on a chunked bulk insert or on BulkUpdate is ErrValidation; an INSERT CTE body over the parameter limit is ErrLimitExceeded Soft delete yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) SoftDelete, ForceDelete, WithDeleted, OnlyDeleted; field tag soft_delete: Optimistic lock, automatic timestamps yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) version column (ErrOptimisticLock); created_at, updated_at tags Typed predicates yes SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet generated columns: Eq, In, IsNull, Lt, ...; And, Or, Not, Like and ILike (always ESCAPE '!', see EscapeLike), ContainsLiteral, Exists; In over the bind limit is ErrValidation Array columns and operators yes: []string maps to text[], also []int16, []int32, []int64, []bool, []float32, []float64, []types.UUID and []uuid.UUID (github.com/google/uuid) (uuid[]); one bind per slice ErrUnsupported at build time arrayop.Contains (@>), arrayop.ContainedBy (<@), arrayop.Overlaps (&&), arrayop.AnyOf (= ANY) Joins yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) Join, LeftJoin, CrossJoin, From Aggregates, GroupBy, Having yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) CountAll, CountOf, CountDistinct, Sum, Avg, Min, Max Projections (non-model result types) yes SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet struct embedding momo.Projection with Columns(...), or generic tuple rows Row1 to Row10; metadata is generated; soft-deleted rows of the From table are filtered Serial ids yes: serial tag, smallserial, serial or bigserial by Go int width refused omitted from inserts and read back with RETURNING; a FromSelect into the table cannot supply ids Keyset pagination yes, non-nullable keys only SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet OrderBy(...).After(values...); the primary key is appended as tie-breaker; nullable key: ErrUnsupported; wrong value count: ErrValidation Streaming yes SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet Each(ctx, fn), Iter(ctx) (iter.Seq2); both ErrUnsupported when the query has Preload Raw SQL yes SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) momo.Exec, momo.Scalars, momo.Query and momo.QueryRows (into a model, a projection, Row1..Row10 or a plain struct scanned by column name with no generated metadata; an unmatched column or field is ErrValidation naming it), momo.SQL, TypedSQL, RawSubquery, Named, In, Ident EXPLAIN yes (EXPLAIN, never ANALYZE) MySQL: ErrUnsupported SelectQuery.Explain(ctx) IndexedBy hint ErrUnsupported; SQLite syntax, run on SQLite in v0.6.0 through sqlitedriver MySQL: ErrUnsupported SelectQuery.IndexedBy

docs.title: Writes, transactions, drivers
docs.text: Feature PostgreSQL SQLite / MySQL Notes RETURNING yes (Returning: true) MySQL: no; MariaDB: INSERT ... RETURNING only (InsertReturning) .Returning(cols...), .ReturningAll() on insert, update, delete; read with .Rows(ctx), or one row with .One(ctx) (ErrNotFound when none came back, ErrTooManyRows for several; every column without a list; ErrUnsupported where RETURNING is; a multi-row Models insert is ErrValidation; MariaDB has no update or delete form in momo). Identity read-back in CreateGraph needs it. INSERT ... SELECT yes: InsertQuery[T].FromSelect with SelectExprs (FROM-less or one source, with Where) or Select[T] as the source; composes with OnConflict, Returning, Upsert[T] SQLite yes (WHERE true is added to a SelectExprs or Select[T] source with FROM and no WHERE before ON CONFLICT); MySQL plain insert only (no ON CONFLICT; FROM-less with WHERE renders FROM DUAL) Target columns are explicit typed columns of T; a select-list count mismatch is ErrValidation. No model hooks, automatic timestamps, Go-side defaults or validators are applied: list those columns yourself. The soft-delete filter on a SelectExprs source needs a TableRef that carries the soft-delete marker. Upsert / ON CONFLICT yes (OnConflict: true) MySQL and MariaDB: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE through the same calls, with the conflict target limited to the only unique key of the table (otherwise ErrUnsupported); see mysql.md Upsert[T] (target = primary key) or InsertQuery[T].OnConflict(cols...).DoNothing() / .DoUpdate(assigns...) with SetExcluded. Upsert neither advances nor checks the version column. OnConflict(...).Where(preds) (partial-index target) and .DoUpdate(...).Where(preds) (conditional update, col.Excluded()): PostgreSQL yes; SQLite: bool, integer, finite float and string values in the target predicate render inline so they match the index expression (golden-tested and run against a real SQLite partial unique index written as WHERE live = 1; the values show up in logs and traces; write index literals as Momo renders them, integers as 2 and floats in plain decimal with .0 for whole numbers for magnitudes from 1e-6 up to 1e21 and exponent form (1e-07, 1e+21) outside that range, otherwise use momo.SQL), any other value or Excluded() there is ErrValidation; MySQL ErrUnsupported. Graph writes yes SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet CreateGraph, FindOrCreate (needs ON CONFLICT), UpsertByPK Merge, BulkUpdate, Truncate yes: Merge is PostgreSQL 15 or later and .Returning needs 17 or later (ErrUnsupported on an older server or a driver without ServerVersioner); BulkUpdate updates only the listed keys (PostgreSQL); Truncate is TRUNCATE TABLE Merge and BulkUpdate: ErrUnsupported. Truncate: SQLite runs DELETE FROM and resets the autoincrement counter; MySQL runs TRUNCATE TABLE (refused inside a transaction) Merge returns ErrValidation when an interceptor adds predicates (deny the kind instead). Truncate runs interceptors with the kind truncate, has no RESTART IDENTITY or CASCADE, and is refused inside a MySQL transaction. Merge does not run field validators on the inserted values Bulk COPY yes: InsertQuery[T].Copy (after Omit, with the models as its argument) on the pgx driver; also momo.CopierOf(querier) for the driver call SQLite and MySQL: Copy returns ErrUnsupported (neither sqlitedriver nor mysqldriver has a Copier) Copy runs the insert interceptors (deny only) and BeforeInsert over a copy of the models; it skips OnConflict, Returning and chunking, and it counts as a write for NewUnitOfWork. On a *DB with WithImplicitTx it runs in its own transaction; on a pinned handle with WithTxSetup it fails closed. Not available through FromSQLDB Batch (several statements, one round trip) driver level: momo.BatcherOf(querier); relation loading uses it automatically SQLite: no (sqlitedriver has no Batcher); MySQL: no (mysqldriver has no Batcher) not available through FromSQLDB Transactions yes: db.Tx(ctx, opts, fn), db.Begin; read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable; read-only SQLite and MySQL: commit, rollback and panic cases run in the shared suite (suite.RunAll); SQLite accepts the default and serializable isolation only (other levels ErrUnsupported) and runs read-only transactions through PRAGMA query_only (sqlitedriver tests) any other sql.IsolationLevel: ErrUnsupported (Op "begin") Savepoints yes: Tx.Savepoint, RollbackTo, Release SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (suite.RunAll) a dialect without savepoints: ErrUnsupported (Op "savepoint") Pinned connection yes: db.OnConn(pc) SQLite and MySQL: the drivers implement Pinner (driver tests); db.OnConn itself is exercised by a MySQL test (generated keys) and not by a SQLite test no transactions on a pinned *DB: Begin, Tx, Replace and CreateGraph fail with ErrUnsupported (Op "begin"), chunked Insert with Op "insert"; Link, Unlink and Count work SET col = DEFAULT, VALUES (DEFAULT) yes SQLite: no DEFAULT in VALUES a multi-row insert that is default in some rows only fails with ErrUnsupported where the dialect cannot express it

docs.title: Row locking, CTEs, subqueries, window functions
docs.text:
Feature PostgreSQL SQLite / MySQL API FOR UPDATE yes (Locking: true) SQLite: ErrUnsupported; MySQL and MariaDB: yes (NOWAIT, SKIP LOCKED; FOR SHARE renders as LOCK IN SHARE MODE on MariaDB) ForUpdate() FOR UPDATE NOWAIT / SKIP LOCKED yes same ForUpdate("NOWAIT"), ForUpdate("SKIP LOCKED") FOR SHARE yes same ForShare() FOR NO KEY UPDATE / FOR KEY SHARE yes, with NOWAIT, SKIP LOCKED and OF SQLite and MySQL: ErrUnsupported ForNoKeyUpdate(), ForKeyShare() FOR UPDATE OF <table> yes; names are quoted aliases or table names SQLite: ErrUnsupported; MySQL: yes; MariaDB: ErrUnsupported ForUpdate("SKIP LOCKED").LockOf("d", "t"); without a lock mode, an unknown or CTE name, NOWAIT together with SKIP LOCKED, or DISTINCT, GROUP BY or HAVING: ErrValidation; Count and Exists keep the lock clause Advisory transaction locks yes: pg_advisory_xact_lock, pg_try_advisory_xact_lock, text keys through hashtext ErrUnsupported advisory.XactLock, advisory.XactLockString, advisory.TryXactLock, advisory.TryXactLockString (package github.com/azrtydxb/momo/advisory, taking the *Tx); a DB does not compile, because a transaction lock outside a transaction is meaningless. docs.text:
The momo migrate command selects the PostgreSQL dialect (see the generated status above for the library dialects). diff, validate (without --db) and hash run offline; the other commands need a database. docs.title: Secrets in errors, hooks and connections
docs.text:
• Argument masking: with WithArgLogging, a value bound from a column tagged sensitive reaches hooks as momo.RedactedArg, not the value. This covers insert values, Set and SetExpr assignments on insert, update and upsert (every argument inside an expression assigned to a sensitive column), the primary-key and version predicates of a model update or delete, keyset After values, and WHERE predicates in which a sensitive column is one operand: the comparison methods, EqExpr and the other expression comparisons, In, NotIn, Between, Like, ILike, ContainsLiteral, arrayop.Contains, arrayop.ContainedBy, arrayop.Overlaps, arrayop.AnyOf, and the same methods on an expression that reads a sensitive column such as sqlfn.Lower of it. Relation loading, Link, Unlink, Replace and Count mask key values bound to sensitive key columns, including join-table columns that map to them. The database still receives the real value. QueryEvent.Args is always a copy, so a hook cannot replace or reorder the bound arguments. The copy is deep for []byte and json.RawMessage values only, so changing those in place does not reach the driver; other mutable argument types are shared. Known gaps: arguments passed to raw momo.SQL or momo.TypedSQL fragments are not masked, because Momo cannot tell which column they belong to; SQLite renders values in an ON CONFLICT target predicate as SQL literals, so such a value appears in QueryEvent.SQL. Do not enable argument logging where raw fragments or conflict-target predicates carry secrets. Error.Detail() is also unmasked: it returns the raw driver detail, which for a PostgreSQL constraint violation quotes the offending key values, including sensitive ones. Do not log it or return it to clients; Error() is the safe text.
  • Encode errors: the pgx driver withholds the text of pgx client-side encode failures, which quote the bound value, on every path (pool, transactions, pinned and adopted connections, the database/sql adapter, rows). The message keeps the argument position, such as args[2]; the original error stays reachable with errors.Is, errors.As and Unwrap. That unwrapped cause still contains the bound value, so code that logs every link of an error chain must not print the causes.
  • Simple protocol: pgxdriver.WithExecMode, FromConnConfig and FromSQLDB refuse simple protocol, which interpolates values client-side, with ErrUnsupported. FromConnConfig checks the config it is given. FromSQLDB cannot read the pgx config of an opaque *sql.DB, so it checks the first connection it uses, on the first statement, not at construction. Only that first connection is checked: a custom connector that varies the exec mode per connection is not checked.

docs.title: Multi-tenant row-level security
docs.text:
Row-level security (RLS) policies usually read a setting such as current_setting('app.tenant_id', true). The fail-closed pattern sets that setting at the start of every transaction from a scope carried in the context.Context, so a statement that forgot its scope matches no rows. WithTxSetup and WithImplicitTx build that into the *DB:

db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool),
    momo.WithTxSetup(func(ctx context.Context, tx *momo.Tx) error {
        id, ok := tenantFrom(ctx)
        if !ok {
            return nil // no scope: nothing is set, the policy matches no rows
        }
        return momo.SetConfigLocal(ctx, tx, "app.tenant_id", id)
    }),
    momo.WithImplicitTx(),
)

ALTER TABLE documents ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE documents FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON documents
  USING (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::bigint)
  WITH CHECK (tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::bigint);

Connect as a role without BYPASSRLS that does not own the tables (or use FORCE, as above): superusers and BYPASSRLS roles skip every policy.

Feature Behavior WithTxSetup The function runs right after every transaction momo begins: DB.Begin, DB.Tx, and the transactions momo opens itself (chunked inserts, graph creation, relation writes, vecsearch.With, implicit transactions). It runs once per real transaction, not per savepoint, and not for AdoptTx (the caller began that transaction). An error rolls back and is returned. WithImplicitTx Auto-commit statements on a *DB (Select, Insert, Update, Delete, Exec, Scalars, relation loads) each run in a short transaction, so the setup applies. Iter, Each and Rows hold the transaction until exhausted or closed, then commit; a scan or driver error rolls back, and so does a cancelled context for a write or a read abandoned early (a fully drained read still commits). Close early-abandoned rows to free the connection. SetConfigLocal set_config(key, value, true): the setting ends with the transaction. The same as Tx.SetLocal. Not used on an implicit *DB Pipelined relation loading (Batch) and the raw driver COPY path, because they bypass the setup (InsertQuery[T].Copy instead runs in its own transaction). BatcherOf and CopierOf report none for such a *DB; use a Tx for them.

A behaviour change for WithImplicitTx on an unpinned *DB only: the rows of an Insert, Update or Delete with RETURNING (Rows) must be read to the end before Close. A write closed unread, or after reading only the first row (for example UpdateQuery.Rows or DeleteQuery.Rows users who read one row and close), is rolled back and Close returns ErrValidation; this includes a panic that unwinds through the loop. Handles without WithImplicitTx, a Tx and a pinned OnConn handle are unaffected, and FindOrCreate, UpsertByPK and CreateGraph read to the end themselves.

Without WithImplicitTx, auto-commit statements on a *DB run outside any transaction, so the setup never applies to them and they are unscoped. Use WithImplicitTx (or DB.Tx) whenever the setup enforces a security boundary. Statements run through db.Driver() bypass momo and its hooks entirely, so they are never scoped either.

The setup does not cover everything. AdoptTx transactions are the caller's, so apply the setting yourself. momo migrate and Go migrations run outside the *DB options, so they are never scoped; run them as a role that may bypass the policies. A handle from OnConn cannot begin a transaction, so on a *DB configured with WithTxSetup its statements fail with ErrUnsupported instead of running unscoped, and it reports no COPY or Batch path. A panic in a setup function rolls the transaction back before it propagates, and a panic in an Each or Iter callback rolls back the implicit transaction. If the context is cancelled before a streaming implicit write is closed, the write is rolled back and Close and Err return the context error.

Behind PgBouncer in transaction mode use only transaction-local settings (SetConfigLocal), never a session-level SET: the session belongs to whichever client PgBouncer hands the backend to next. TestImplicitTxPgBouncer runs concurrent tenants through PgBouncer and checks no scope leaks.

docs.title: PgBouncer and TLS
docs.text: Feature PostgreSQL Notes PgBouncer, transaction pooling yes, with the default exec mode The default pgx.QueryExecModeExec sends unnamed statements and binds server-side. TestPgBouncerNoNamedPreparedStatements checks on the wire that no named prepared statement is created. WithExecMode also accepts CacheStatement, CacheDescribe, DescribeExec; the simple protocol is rejected with ErrUnsupported. Do not run momo migrate through a transaction pooler. A search_path set at connection start does not reliably survive pooling; vecsearch.Settings and Tx.SetLocal use transaction-local set_config, which does. TLS yes, as configured by the pgx connection string (sslmode, sslrootcert, ...) NewPool(ctx, url) hands the URL to pgx. Momo adds no TLS options. momo migrate prints a TLS warning when the URL has sslmode=disable and a non-loopback host. Use sslmode=verify-full for remote databases.

docs.title: What returns ErrUnsupported
docs.text:
All match errors.Is(err, momo.ErrUnsupported). Build-time errors surface from SQL() or at first execution.

Call When momo migrate on SQLite or MySQL The CLI builds only the PostgreSQL dialect, so momo migrate exits 2 on both (use the library dialects migrate/sqlite and migrate/mysql) Upsert, OnConflict, FindOrCreate Upsert, OnConflict: a dialect with neither ON CONFLICT nor ON DUPLICATE KEY; on MySQL also a target that is not the only unique key, and a Where on the conflict clause. FindOrCreate: a dialect without ON CONFLICT and RETURNING, which is MySQL and MariaDB CreateGraph *Tx on a dialect without savepoints; dialect without RETURNING (rejected before the transaction opens) ForUpdate, ForShare dialect without row locks (SQLite metadata) IndexedBy PostgreSQL and MySQL After a nullable OrderBy key SetDefault, multi-row insert with default in some rows dialect without DEFAULT support for that shape db.Begin, db.Tx, Replace, CreateGraph, chunked insert *DB pinned with OnConn (Op "begin"; chunked insert: Op "insert"); unknown Querier; isolation level outside the four standard ones Tx.Savepoint dialect without savepoints (Op "savepoint") Each, Iter the query has Preload Joined() not belongs-to, child key not unique, GroupBy, Having, row locks, Each, Iter, or combined with Load, LoadAll, Scope, Then LoadPerParentLimit belongs-to or has-one relation Link, Unlink, Replace, Count belongs-to relation Vector builders metric the dialect lacks (inner product and Jaccard on SQLite), or the driver reports Vectors: false vecsearch.Apply, vecsearch.With pgvector missing or older than 0.8.0 when an iterative, max_scan_tuples, scan_mem_multiplier or max_probes field is set; any non-ExactSearch field on SQLite; transaction-scoped settings on a non-PostgreSQL dialect SelectQuery.Explain MySQL and MariaDB Migration inspect or apply missing extension (for example vector): the error names it; unsupported object on inspect pgxdriver.WithExecMode simple protocol or any unlisted mode: every query returns it pgxdriver.FromSQLDB nil db, or a db not backed by the pgx stdlib driver (every Query, Exec, Begin and Pin then fails). A valid FromSQLDB driver can Pin, but the pinned connection has no Batch or COPY Generator type mapping Go type with no SQL mapping on the dialect (gen/typemap) Batch, COPY a pinned connection without a batch or COPY path (Op "batch", "copy"); WithExecMode differing from the connection's default exec mode makes the pgx batch fail (Op "batch"). Relation loading falls back to sequential on its own in both cases; a FromSQLDB pinned connection has no Batcher and loads sequentially

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: The contributor guide is the CONTRIBUTING.md file at the repository root, included here so the site and the repository stay in sync.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go 1.26 or later
  • A C toolchain (for the SQLite packages, which use cgo)
  • Docker (for make db-up, the local integration databases)

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
• make test: unit tests, including the separate module internal/integration that holds the tests needing gqlgen, gRPC, protoc or the OpenAPI validator
  • make test-race: unit tests with the race detector
  • make test-compilefail: compile-fail tests for the typed API
  • make test-integration: integration tests against real databases

Every test that needs a database lives in a file that starts with the //go:build integration tag, next to the SPDX line, and gets its database from internal/testdb or testopen. make test, and the macOS and Windows CI jobs, build without the tag and so run unit tests only; they cannot skip a database test silently because they never compile one. make test-integration sets MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1, so an unset database URL fails the run. TestIntegrationTagConvention in internal/repocheck fails when a file that uses these helpers lacks the tag.

Fuzz targets are listed in FUZZ_TARGETS in the Makefile and make test-fuzz runs each one for FUZZTIME, an execution count. TestFuzzTargetsListed fails when a Fuzz function is missing from the list.

Dialect coverage is expressed as subtests from testopen.Each, one per dialect built into this version; integration tests have no name suffix. make test-integration-<dialect> sets that dialect's URL variables and runs the whole suite.

docs.title: Documentation pages and Go code blocks
docs.text:
A new page under docs/ must be added to the nav in mkdocs.yml and linked from docs/README.md; TestEveryDocPageInNav and TestDocsIndexLinksEveryPage fail otherwise. Every Go block in docs/ is checked by TestDocsCodeBlocks: write a complete package main program (it is compiled), or, for a snippet that cannot stand alone, put the comment <!-- docscheck:fragment --> on the line before the fence (it must still parse as Go). The number of fragments is capped by maxFragmentBlocks in internal/docscheck/codeblocks_test.go, so prefer a program. A block marked <!-- docscheck:run --> is also executed against PostgreSQL.

An identifier in a backticked span is checked by TestDocsIdentifiersResolve: pkg.Name must exist. A bare name such as Select means the root momo package. When only a feature package exports it (Case is in sqlfn), TestBareNamesAreRootNames fails with the file, the line and the suggestion sqlfn.Case; write the qualified name; the same holds for a method such as migrate.Engine.Apply. A collision in prose is fixed by qualifying, never by removing the backticks. A page whose section names the package may keep bare names if internal/docscheck/testdata/bare_allow.txt lists the page and the package with a reason.

docs.title: Exported API changes need a docs change
docs.text:
The apidiff-docs CI job (make apidiff-gate, scripts/apidiff-docs-gate.sh) runs golang.org/x/exp/cmd/apidiff, pinned in the Makefile, between the base branch and your branch for the root package and every non-internal subpackage. Any exported change, compatible or incompatible, fails the job unless one of two things holds:

  • the diff touches README.md, llms.txt, a Markdown page under docs/ (docs/**/*.md) or an examples/**/README.md (other files under docs/ and examples/ do not count); or
  • the pull request body, or a commit message in the range, has a line that starts in column 0 with Docs: no reader-visible change: followed by a real reason, for example Docs: no reader-visible change: internal helper exposed for tests. A blank reason, a <placeholder> such as <reason>, and an indented or quoted line are rejected.

A change to a Go comment or an unexported identifier produces an empty report and needs neither. The job lives in its own workflow, .github/workflows/apidiff-docs.yml, so it also runs when the PR body is edited: add the escape line to the body and the check re-evaluates without a new commit. The job reads the live body, not the stale event payload. It keeps one comment (marked <!-- apidiff-docs -->) with the apidiff report, and posts none when the API did not change. Run it locally with make apidiff-gate.

docs.title: Root package file names
docs.text: Every non-test .go file in the repository root is doc.go or is named with one of the prefixes db, tx, driver, err, build, meta, expr, col, select, insert, update, delete, upsert, write, raw or rel, either bare (db.go) or followed by an underscore and a topic (expr_ops.go). A test file is named after its subject file where it has one (foo_test.go, foo_internal_test.go or foo_integration_test.go for a subject foo.go; a longer topic such as foo_bar_integration_test.go is fine). The guard checks only the prefix: a test file's name without _test must itself start with one of the prefixes, and a test that spans several files takes the prefix of the area it tests. TestRootFilePrefixes in internal/repocheck fails on any other name and lists the prefixes in its message. There is no exception list: rename the file instead.

docs.title: Commit messages and PR titles
docs.text: Commit messages and PR titles use Conventional Commits: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert. Mark breaking changes with feat!: or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

docs.title: SPDX headers
docs.text:
Every new .go file starts with this header, followed by a blank line before package:

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

package example

Generated files begin with // Code generated by momo instead.

docs.title: Full-text search
docs.text: PostgreSQL full-text search has a column type and typed expressions in Momo. Every builder here returns ErrUnsupported when the statement is built for SQLite or MySQL.

docs.title: The column
docs.text:
A model field of type types.TSVector maps to a tsvector column (and a types.TSQuery field to tsquery). Both are codecs, so the generator and migrate pick the column type from the Go type, diff it and read it back from the database with no drift. The Go value is the text form PostgreSQL prints, for example 'cat':3 'fat':2. A nullable column is a *types.TSVector.

The application normally never sets this column (leave it nil on insert and update: the trigger overwrites it). Keep it current with a trigger declared in MomoConfig, and index it with GIN:

type Article struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:kb_articles"`
    ID         int64            `momo:"pk,identity"`
    Title      string
    Body       string
    SearchTsv  *types.TSVector
    Embedding  vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"`
}

func (a *Article) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
    c.Index("kb_articles_search_gin", &a.SearchTsv).Method("gin")
    c.Function(schema.Function{
        Name: "kb_articles_tsv", Returns: "trigger", Language: "plpgsql", Volatility: "VOLATILE",
        Body: "BEGIN NEW.search_tsv := setweight(to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.title, '')), 'A') || " +
            "to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.body, '')); RETURN NEW; END;",
    })
    c.Trigger(schema.Trigger{
        Table: "kb_articles", Name: "kb_articles_tsv_trg", Timing: "BEFORE",
        Events: []string{"INSERT", "UPDATE"}, ForEachRow: true, Function: "kb_articles_tsv()",
    })
}

docs.title: Expressions
docs.text:
The builders live in the package github.com/azrtydxb/momo/fts. They used to be functions of the root package; see upgrading for the name table.

The text search configuration (english, simple, ...) is a string. It is bound as a parameter and cast to regconfig, so it cannot carry SQL; an empty one fails the build with ErrValidation.

Builder SQL Result type fts.Match vec @@ query Predicate fts.ToVector to_tsvector(config, text) fts.Expr[types.TSVector] fts.WebsearchToQuery websearch_to_tsquery(config, text) fts.Expr[types.TSQuery] fts.PlainToQuery plainto_tsquery(config, text) fts.Expr[types.TSQuery] fts.PhraseToQuery phraseto_tsquery(config, text) fts.Expr[types.TSQuery] fts.ToQuery to_tsquery(config, text) fts.Expr[types.TSQuery] fts.Rank ts_rank(vec, query [, normalization]) fts.Expr[float64] fts.RankCD ts_rank_cd(vec, query [, normalization]) fts.Expr[float64] fts.Headline ts_headline(config, text, query [, options]) fts.Expr[string]

The query text, the configuration and the headline options are always bound parameters. The normalization argument of the rank functions is the optional PostgreSQL flag mask (0 to 63) and renders as a literal. fts.WebsearchToQuery accepts any user input without raising a syntax error, so it is the builder for a search box; fts.ToQuery expects tsquery syntax and a malformed query is a database error.

An fts.Expr has As, Asc, Desc and the comparison methods of any scalar expression, so it works in Where, OrderBy and Columns:

q := fts.WebsearchToQuery("english", userInput)
rank := fts.RankCD(articleSearch, q)

hits, err := momo.Select[Hit](db).
    From(momo.TableRef{Name: "kb_articles"}).
    Columns(articleID, rank.As("rank"),
        fts.Headline("english", articleBody, q, "StartSel=<b>, StopSel=</b>, MaxFragments=2")).
    Where(fts.Match(articleSearch, q)).
    OrderBy(rank.Desc()).
    Limit(20).
    All(ctx)

Here articleSearch is a Column[types.TSVector] and articleBody a Column[string]. Without a stored column, search a text column directly with fts.ToVector over articleBody as the first operand of fts.Match (an expression index on the same expression keeps it fast).

Every use of a call binds its own parameters (the configuration and the query text), so the same expression written in the select list and again in GROUP BY gets different placeholders, and PostgreSQL rejects the statement as an ungrouped column. The same applies to SELECT DISTINCT with an ORDER BY on the call. Group by a stored tsvector instead, or compute the call once in a subquery or CTE and refer to its alias. A golden test pins the placeholders.

Arguments bound by these calls are masked in hook events (shown as RedactedArg) when an operand reads a column marked sensitive; the driver still receives the real values.

docs.title: Hybrid ranking: vector plus text
docs.text:
For reciprocal rank fusion of the two signals, use momo.HybridSearch (see hybrid search). To weigh the signals yourself, combine them in one score with the typed arithmetic helpers. The cosine distance is lower for better matches and the text rank is higher, so subtract a weighted rank from the distance and order ascending:

dist := vecop.Cosine(articleEmb, queryEmbedding) // vector.Vector
text := fts.RankCD(articleSearch, fts.WebsearchToQuery("english", userInput))
score := sqlfn.SubExpr[float64](dist, sqlfn.Mul[float64](text, 0.5))

hits, err := momo.Select[Hit](db).
    From(momo.TableRef{Name: "kb_articles"}).
    Columns(articleID, score.As("score"), articleTitle).
    OrderBy(score.Asc()).
    Limit(20).
    All(ctx)

This scores every row. To restrict the candidate set to text matches, add a Where on fts.Match over articleSearch and the same query, which lets the GIN index prune the rows before the vector distance is computed. The TestFullTextHybridRanking integration test runs this pattern.

docs.title: Scanning
docs.text: pgx returns tsvector and tsquery values as text, which types.TSVector and types.TSQuery scan. ts_rank and ts_rank_cd return real; they scan into float64 fields.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page takes you from an empty module to a program that talks to PostgreSQL through Momo. It stays small on purpose: the first program uses no generated code. The full loop (models, momo generate, migrations, typed queries, relations, vector search) is the quickstart example, which is compiled and run end to end in CI.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Go 1.26 or newer.
  • PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension installed on the server. The other databases, and the dialects the momo migrate command runs, are listed in the generated status of capabilities.
  • A role that may create extensions, or a superuser who runs CREATE EXTENSION vector once in the target database. The first generated migration creates the extension when a model has a vector column.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Add the library to your module and install the CLI at the same version:

go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@latest
go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo@latest

Pin an explicit version instead of latest in a real project, and keep the CLI and the library on the same one. The supported Go and PostgreSQL versions are listed in supported versions.

docs.title: Connect and run SQL
docs.text:
pgxdriver.NewPool opens a pgx pool, pgxdriver.New wraps it as a Momo driver and momo.New returns the *momo.DB. db.Tx runs a function in a transaction and commits when it returns nil. Inside it, use the tx handle for every statement. momo.Exec and momo.Scalars are the raw SQL path: ? binds the next argument, so values never become part of the SQL text.

The program reads the connection string from MOMO_EXAMPLE_DSN, for example postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/scratch?sslmode=disable. It creates a temporary table inside the transaction, so it leaves nothing behind.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
)

func main() {
    if err := run(context.Background()); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}

func run(ctx context.Context) error {
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("MOMO_EXAMPLE_DSN"))
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer pool.Close()
    db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))

    return db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
        if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "CREATE TEMP TABLE notes (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, body text NOT NULL)"); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "INSERT INTO notes (id, body) VALUES (?, ?)", 1, "hello"); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        bodies, err := momo.Scalars[string](ctx, tx, "SELECT body FROM notes WHERE id = ?", 1)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        fmt.Println(bodies)
        return nil
    })
}

docs.title: Handle errors
docs.text:
Momo classifies database errors into sentinels. Compare with errors.Is, never with error text. This program violates a primary key on purpose and branches on momo.ErrUniqueViolation; the transaction rolls back when the function returns the error, so the table disappears with it.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "errors"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("MOMO_EXAMPLE_DSN"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer pool.Close()
    db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))

    err = db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
        if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "CREATE TEMP TABLE tags (name text PRIMARY KEY)"); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        for range 2 {
            if _, err := momo.Exec(ctx, tx, "INSERT INTO tags (name) VALUES (?)", "go"); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
        return nil
    })
    if !errors.Is(err, momo.ErrUniqueViolation) {
        log.Fatalf("want a unique violation, got %v", err)
    }
    fmt.Println("duplicate rejected")
}

Every Go block in these docs is checked in CI: a block is either a complete package main program that must compile, a program marked as runnable (this one runs against PostgreSQL on every build), or an explicitly marked fragment that must still parse as Go.

docs.title: Typed queries
docs.text:
Typed queries need generated code. You describe a table as a struct that embeds momo.Model, run momo generate, and build queries from the generated descriptors, so a misspelled column or a wrong value type fails at compile time:

momo generate
momo migrate diff init
momo migrate apply

The quickstart example shows the models, the momo.yaml configuration, the generated packages and the first migration. Then read:

  • Agent guide: the complete reference in one file, from tags to errors, with the pitfalls.
  • Type mapping: the column type for each Go type.
  • Migrations: what momo migrate does and how to recover.
  • Relations, projections and vector search.

docs.title: Importing models from other ORMs
docs.text:
Momo can read the models of an existing GORM, Bun or Ent project and write the equivalent Momo structs. Three packages do the reading:

Package Reads importer/gorm GORM structs and their gorm:"..." tags, gorm.Model importer/bun Bun structs and their bun:"..." tags importer/ent the Ent schema package (fields, edges, indexes, mixins)

Each package exports one function, Read(dir string), that returns the neutral []importer.Model and an *importer.Report. importer.Emit turns the models into Momo source through the generator's writer.

The readers are static. They parse the Go files of dir with go/parser and never compile, load or execute your code, so reading a project cannot run its init functions, hooks or migrations. The flip side is that they see only what is written as a literal in those files: a naming strategy set in another package, or an index added by a migration, is not visible. Each reader's package comment lists its limits.

docs.title: The momo import command
docs.text:
momo import gorm --src ./old/models --out ./models
momo import bun  --src ./old/models --out ./models --report import-report.txt
momo import ent  --src ./ent/schema --out ./models --package models

The command runs the reader, prints the import report to standard output and writes the Momo structs to <out>/models.go with a generated-file header. --package sets the Go package name (the default is derived from --out), and --report also writes the report to a file.

Exit codes: 0 the models were written, 1 the report holds an unsupported change and nothing was written, 2 a usage or input error. Fix or convert the listed constructs by hand, or remove them from the source, and run it again. The command never overwrites a file that does not carry the generated-file header.

docs.title: Importing migration history
docs.text:
The importer/history package converts the migration history of another tool into a Momo migration directory, so a database that already ran those migrations does not run them again. Four readers produce the input:

Package Reads importer/history/atlas an Atlas directory (<version>_<name>.sql, atlas.sum) and the rows of atlas_schema_revisions importer/history/goose a goose directory and the goose_db_version table importer/history/golangmigrate <version>_<title>.up.sql and .down.sql files and schema_migrations importer/history/bun Bun's SQL migrations and the bun_migrations table

Each package exports Read, which returns a history.Source. history.Convert refuses a source that is dirty, that holds migrations the tool never applied, or that holds migrations it cannot convert (Bun and goose Go-function migrations). A source version that is not a 14-digit timestamp is mapped to 19700101000000 plus its position in the list, and the mapping is reported as a version-mapped change; the original version stays in the history name column. history.Baseline replays the converted SQL on an empty scratch database to write one schema snapshot per migration, history.WriteImport writes the directory and history.HistoryRows gives the momo_migrations rows that mark every migration as applied. The Atlas reader verifies atlas.sum with Atlas's directory hash and refuses a directory whose files were edited. golang-migrate records only its current version, so every migration up to it is read as applied.

docs.title: The import report
docs.text:
A Momo model is never an exact copy of an ORM model, because the ORMs differ in behaviour you do not see in the struct: GORM replaces a zero value with the column default, Ent saves an edge only when its setter was called, and so on. The importer does not paper over these differences. Every one becomes a importer.Change in the report, with the source position (file:line:col), the model, the field and a message. importer.Report.String() prints one line per change, sorted by position, in the form source: kind: Model.Field: message.

Read the report before you trust the converted models. importer.Report.Has(kind) and importer.Report.Of(kind) filter it in code. The kinds are:

Kind Meaning zero-value-handling the source ORM treats a zero value as unset and applies a default; Momo writes the zero value (use a pointer to leave it unset) implicit-save the source ORM saves an association together with its parent; Momo writes only the model you pass go-default the source ORM computes a default in Go (timestamps, generated values); Momo needs a tag or a database default unsupported something the reader cannot convert (an unreadable tag, an unknown builder call, a type with no mapping); convert it by hand renamed-type the field type changes on import, for example gorm.DeletedAt becomes *time.Time, and the automatic filter does not carry over dropped-field a field that does not become a column (ignored with -, scan-only, relation fields) is not imported dropped-index an index Momo's tags cannot express (a composite index, a second index tag on a field) is not imported; declare it in the companion file naming a table, column, constraint or foreign key name that Momo derives itself, or a naming strategy the reader cannot see; check the names version-mapped a migration version was renumbered while importing migration history (importer/history) go-side-rule a validator, immutable field, hook or policy that the source ORM runs in Go and Momo does not

The importer never drops one of these silently: an empty report means the reader found nothing to flag, not that it checked behaviour it cannot see.

docs.title: Migration safety and recovery
docs.text:
Momo v0.6.0, PostgreSQL (SQLite and MySQL as libraries, sections 3a and 9). Every statement here was checked against migrate/, cli/, schema/ and dialect/; the tests that pin a behavior are named. For the first run see README, Create and apply the migration.

With a dialect the momo migrate command does not link, it exits 2 ("migrations for dialect ... are not available yet"). The library migration dialects are described in section 3a (SQLite) and section 9 (MySQL and MariaDB):

A database is usable when a driver package for it exists under driver/:

  • PostgreSQL: usable through driver/pgxdriver (vector builders: yes). Migrations: migrate/postgres, run by momo migrate.
  • SQLite: usable through driver/sqlitedriver (needs cgo, not on Windows, vector builders: yes) and driver/sqlitepure (vector builders: no). Migrations: migrate/sqlite, library only (momo migrate does not select it).
  • MySQL and MariaDB: usable through driver/mysqldriver (vector storage and builders depend on the server version). Migrations: migrate/mysql, library only (momo migrate does not select it).

docs.title: 1. Model
docs.text:
models (Go structs) --momo migrate diff--> <v>_<name>.up.sql + <v>_<name>.snapshot.json + momo.sum
                                              |
database <--------momo migrate apply---------+  (history table: momo_migrations)

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
All files live in one directory per dialect (default migrations/postgres, set migrate.dir.postgres or --dir). diff writes exactly three files:

File Content <version>_<name>.up.sql Statements. Header -- momo:generated, plus -- momo:destructive and/or -- momo:no-transaction when needed. Statements are separated by a blank line and each ends in ;. <version>_<name>.snapshot.json The whole schema after this migration, wrapped as {format_version, version, parent, schema}. schema carries its own format_version. momo.sum Checksum manifest of every file in the directory, rewritten by diff.
  • version is a 14-digit UTC timestamp (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS). If the clock is not past the latest existing version, diff uses the second after it, so versions only grow.
  • name must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.
  • .down.sql files are optional and hand-written (diff never generates one). They are hashed in momo.sum, and apply never runs them. Only Engine.Rollback runs them (section 2).
  • Files whose name starts with . are ignored everywhere (.DS_Store, .momo-*.tmp). A symlink to a directory inside the migration directory is an error. Moving an applied file into a subdirectory is fine: history is keyed by version, not path (TestMovingAppliedMigrationIntoArchiveKeepsHistory).
  • diff never overwrites a file (exit 1 if one exists) and writes all-or-none: temporaries first, then publish, momo.sum last.

docs.title: Format versions
docs.text:
Artifact Field v0.6.0 value Newer than this binary Snapshot wrapper format_version 1 read error, "upgrade momo" Embedded schema schema.format_version 1 read error, "upgrade momo" momo.sum header # momo.sum format=N 1 read error History table checksum of the row __momo_meta__ 1 apply refuses, "upgrade momo"

A snapshot without format_version is rejected.

docs.title: Diff
docs.text:
momo migrate diff <name> runs offline (no database, no driver). It loads the models, compares them with the snapshot of the highest version in the directory (the empty schema when there is none), orders the changes by dependency and renders SQL. No difference: prints no changes, exit 0, writes nothing.

  • Renames are never guessed. A drop plus an add prints a hint: possible rename ...; pass --rename-table old=new or --rename-column table.old=new.
  • Dropped extensions and schemas are not dropped in the database; diff prints a hint that they are no longer managed.
  • Diff never reads the database. A table that is already populated is indistinguishable from an empty one (see section 5).

diff does not depend on momo generate. momo generate --check verifies only the generated *_gen.go files (exit 1 and stale: <path> lines when stale). There is no momo migrate diff --check. To fail CI when the models have no migration, run momo migrate diff ci_probe on a clean checkout and fail unless it prints no changes (when there is a difference it writes files and exits 0, so also check git status --porcelain on the migration directory). This recipe is derived from the code, not covered by a test.

docs.title: Checksums
docs.text:
Two independent checks, both SHA-256 of the file bytes:

  1. momo.sum must match the directory: every file present, none added, removed or changed. Engine.Apply, Status and Baseline refuse otherwise (ErrChecksumMismatch, naming the files). A missing momo.sum is an error that names momo migrate hash. momo.sum itself carries a directory hash; a hand-edited momo.sum is rejected.
  2. The history row of an applied migration stores the checksum of its up file. Engine.Apply refuses when that file changed since (the error says ... changed after version V was applied).

Plan and Drift do not check either.

docs.title: History table
docs.text:
momo_migrations. Every statement against it (read, insert, update, delete and the CREATE TABLE) names the table schema-qualified and quoted, for example "app"."momo_migrations". The table is resolved before the lock is taken, and again right after, and the advisory-lock key is built from that resolved schema, so a migration that changes search_path cannot redirect the history writes. If the two lookups disagree (another process created the table in an earlier schema in between), the lock is released and the attempt is repeated once; a second disagreement fails with an error asking you to retry.

  • An existing table is found the way earlier versions found it, through the session search_path, and its schema is then used. Installs made with the unqualified name keep working, and no second table is created.
  • The resolved object must be a regular, permanent table, and the connecting role must be its owner or hold the privileges of the owning role (pg_has_role with USAGE, so a role with NOINHERIT does not qualify). A superuser holds every role's privileges, so a superuser migrator additionally requires the owner to be itself or another superuser; a table owned by an ordinary role is refused, because its triggers and rules would run with superuser rights. A view, foreign table, unlogged or temporary table, or a table owned by an unrelated role, named momo_migrations earlier on the search_path, is refused with a validation error naming the schema, the table and the owner; it is never used. A table adopted on first install by CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS passes the same checks after the statement runs.
  • What this does and does not defend: it stops a foreign-owned or non-table object that sits ahead of the real table on the search_path from capturing the history writes. It does not stop a role whose privileges you hold, or another superuser, from owning such an object, and it cannot protect a schema that other roles may write to and that is ahead of yours on the search_path before any table exists. Keep schemas on the migrator's search_path writable only by the migrator.
  • With no table yet, it is created in the current schema. migrate.Config.Schemas[0] (migrate.schemas) must equal the current schema (current_schema) or the engine returns a configuration error naming both. plan, status and drift on a connection with no current schema and no table report an empty history; apply and the other writers fail.
  • momo does not SET search_path for the migration session. Migrations are written against the search_path of the connection you give momo and may rely on it; qualify the history table, not the migrations. Set the search_path in the connection URL, and pin it per role with ALTER ROLE on the migrator role.
Column Type Meaning version TEXT PRIMARY KEY Migration version name TEXT Migration name checksum TEXT SHA-256 of the up file status TEXT running, applied, failed, rolled_back (and meta) statements_applied INTEGER Statements that completed error TEXT Failure text, empty on success applied_at TEXT RFC 3339 UTC execution_ms BIGINT Duration apply_id TEXT UTC timestamp plus 8 hex digits, shared by one apply run; baseline for baselined rows kind TEXT sql (default), or go for a Go migration (section 6a)

One extra row, version = '__momo_meta__', status = 'meta', holds the history format version. ReadHistory and Inspect hide it and the table. running and failed are "dirty". rolled_back is not dirty.

docs.title: How apply decides what to run
docs.text:
1. Take the migration lock, set session timeouts, create the history table if missing.
  2. Refuse (ErrDirty, exit 3) if any row is running or failed.
  3. Refuse (ErrChecksumMismatch, exit 3) on a checksum problem (above).
  4. Pending = every *.up.sql and every registered Go migration (section 6a) whose version has no row other than rolled_back, run in ascending version order, optionally stopping after --to N (a version without a file is refused, so a typo applies nothing).

The test is "has no row", not "is newer than the latest applied". An older file that appears later (a merged branch) is still applied, after newer ones. apply does not check snapshot parents; validate does (section 2).

docs.title: Drift
docs.text:
momo migrate drift inspects the live database and compares it with the snapshot of the latest applied migration (the empty schema if none, so every object is unmanaged). Exit 0 and no drift, or exit 1 and one line per finding:

Line Meaning changed: <kind> <name>: <detail> In both, definition differs. A column, index or constraint present only live is changed: ... not in snapshot on that object. An invalid index is changed: ... invalid index (failed CONCURRENTLY build). missing: <kind> <name> In the snapshot, not in the database. unmanaged: <kind> <name> In the database, not in the snapshot: tables, views, functions, enums, schemas, extensions (every extension except plpgsql, for example pg_stat_statements, pgcrypto), and triggers/policies on managed tables. unverified: <kind> <name> Not compared and does not affect the exit code (below).
  • Extension versions are ignored when either side leaves the version empty.
  • Hide objects you do not manage with migrate.exclude (globs over name or schema.name; they apply to tables, views, functions, enums, extensions, triggers and policies). Example: exclude: ["pg_stat_statements", "audit_*"]. PostgreSQL inspection applies the globs while it reads, before an object is examined: a matching table is skipped before its columns, constraints, indexes and partitions are read, a matching view or function before its definition is read, and a trigger whose own name or table matches before its definition is read. So an object the schema model cannot represent (for example a table with a VIRTUAL generated column) no longer fails generate --from-db, baseline or drift once you exclude it. Extensions, enums and policies are not skipped early; they are filtered afterwards as before. generate --from-db also passes every introspect.skip glob to inspection the same way, so a skipped table is never read (the globs also match views and functions of that name).
  • migrate.Config.OnlyTables (set from introspect.only by the CLI) is the inverse for tables: when it is not empty, a table whose name or schema.name matches none of its globs is not managed. A table in the current schema is matched by its bare name only (its schema is empty), so write users, not public.users, when public is the current schema. Inspection does not read it (migrate.InspectOptions.Only, honoured by the PostgreSQL inspector), and drift, baseline and diff hide it, with its triggers and policies, like an excluded table. migrate.MatchObject(globs, schemaName, name) is the matching rule Exclude, OnlyTables and the inspector share. An empty entry is an error. diff filters both sides: a snapshot table outside OnlyTables never plans DROP TABLE, and a model for one never plans CREATE TABLE: a model for a table outside only is never migrated. Partition children are tables of their own: only: [orders] leaves out orders_2024; use only: [orders, "orders_*"]. The MySQL and SQLite inspectors ignore InspectOptions.Only and read every table; the filter is applied afterwards, so a table they cannot represent can still fail inspection.
  • A trigger limited to some columns (AFTER UPDATE OF state) is schema.Trigger.UpdateOf: PostgreSQL renders UPDATE OF "state", inspection reads the list back and generate --from-db writes it into the model.
  • momo_migrations is never reported.
  • A view query, trigger WHEN and policy USING/WITH CHECK changed outside migrations is reported as changed: (the detail names query, when, using or check), and a body declared in another spelling than the server reports (id>0 against id > 0) is not drift. To compare them, drift rewrites the snapshot's text through a scratch schema in a rolled-back transaction (the same step as baseline), which needs CREATE on the database and a writable session. No DDL runs against the application schema (TestDriftBodiesRunsDDLOnlyInRolledBackTransaction).
  • A role that cannot do that (a read-only CI role, say) still gets a report: the bodies are listed as unverified: <kind> <name> and do not affect the exit code, so exit 0 does not prove they match. momo migrate drift --strict (Engine.DriftWith(ctx, DriftOptions{Strict: true})) turns that case into an error: exit 3 with a message wrapping ErrCanonicalizePrivilege that names the privilege. Use --strict where a clean report must mean the policies were checked, since a policy loosened to USING (true) hides in unverified: otherwise (TestDriftBodiesNeedCreateOnDatabase, both modes, as momo_app). Function bodies are compared in both modes.
  • A snapshot without those bodies canonicalizes only its table text (defaults, checks, index predicates) through the same scratch schema. There drift stays tolerant: without CREATE it still runs and can show false changed entries (never hides a real one), and lists the tables it compared as declared in CanonicalizeSkipped.

docs.title: 2. CLI
docs.text:
momo has four commands: generate, migrate, viz, help. Global exit codes: 0 success, 1 findings, 2 usage/config, 3 database/lock/execution (migrate).

Shared flags on every migrate subcommand: --config/-c momo.yaml, --dir, --dialect, --url.

Command Needs DB Does Exit 1 when diff <name> [--rename-table a=b]... [--rename-column t.a=b]... [--allow-destructive] [--stage] [--enforce-not-null] no Write a migration (section 1, 5). destructive or staged refusal; target file exists; model diagnostics plan yes List pending migrations with statement counts. Read-only, no lock, creates nothing. never apply [--to N] [--lock-wait 30s] yes Apply pending. a chain refusal (ErrBranchConflict, ErrChainInvalid, ErrOutOfOrder); other failures are 3 status yes One line per version: applied, pending, dirty, mismatch, missing. Read-only. any version not applied/pending validate [--db] no (--db yes) Directory checks (below); --db adds status. any problem or unhealthy status hash no Recompute momo.sum, list files it accepts as changed:/added:/removed:, write it. never new --custom <name> no Write an empty hand-written migration (section 6). a file would be overwritten baseline --version N [--force] yes Record migrations through N as applied without running them (section 7). database differs from snapshot drift [--strict] yes Section 1. any change, missing or unmanaged resolve --version N --applied or --rolled-back yes Settle a dirty migration (section 4). never rehash --version N [--accept] yes Show, and with --accept store, the new checksum of an edited applied migration (section 4). without --accept, when the file differs lint [--db] no (--db yes) Report risky operations with a safer alternative (section 5). a finding has severity error (warnings alone exit 0) rollback [--group] [--lock-wait 30s] yes Run the .down.sql of the last applied migration, or of its group. a version has no down file (ErrNoDown) or is a Go migration rebase --onto <dir> [name] no Regenerate this branch's generated migrations on top of <dir> (section 4). the result is not a valid chain, or a branch file is hand-written

validate checks: files parse and directives are known; momo.sum matches; versions unique and increasing; each snapshot's parent exists; no two snapshots share a parent (branch conflict); each up file has a snapshot; a hand-written migration (no -- momo:generated) has a snapshot equal to its parent's. Use it in CI. apply runs the chain checks too (fork, missing parent, cycle, gap) and refuses with the same message (a fork is ErrBranchConflict; a missing parent, cycle or gap is ErrChainInvalid; both exit 1, like validate findings), and it refuses with ErrOutOfOrder (exit 1) when a pending version is older than the latest applied one, so a late-merged older migration is never applied after newer ones (TestApplyRefusesForkedChain, TestApplyRefusesPendingOlderThanApplied, TestApplyRefusesBrokenChain, TestMigrateChainRefusalsExitOne).

Recovering from ErrBranchConflict or ErrOutOfOrder. Both mean two teammates branched from the same snapshot and both merged: two snapshots share a parent, and one of the new migrations has a version older than the other. Fix it in the files of the branch that merged last, before it is applied anywhere. The late migration is still pending, so it needs no rehash:

With a checkout of the target branch's migration directory (Momo has no git dependency, so make it with git archive or a second checkout), momo migrate rebase --onto <dir> [name] does steps 1 and 2 below in one command and validates the result. It refuses, naming the file, a branch migration without -- momo:generated or with a hand-written .down.sql, and a target directory that is not a valid chain. --onto takes a directory only. The branch directory must hold every migration of the target, as after a merge; the command prints problem: lines and exits 1 when it does not. By hand:

  1. Delete its <version>_<name>.up.sql and <version>_<name>.snapshot.json (a generated migration; for a hand-written one rename the .up.sql to a version later than the newest applied one and copy the newest snapshot to the same new version, with parent set to the previous snapshot).
  2. Run momo migrate diff <name>. It compares the models with the latest snapshot and writes the migration again with a new version and the right parent.
  3. Run momo migrate hash, review the changed:/added:/removed: list, and run momo migrate validate.

If the older migration was already applied somewhere, do not rewrite it: leave the chain as it is and add a new migration for the difference.

momo migrate new --custom <name> writes an empty hand-written migration (section 6).

  • momo migrate rollback [--group] (Engine.Rollback(ctx, RollbackOptions{Group: false})) runs the .down.sql of the last applied migration (the applied row with the greatest applied_at); with Group: true it runs the downs of every row that shares the greatest apply_id, in descending version order. It takes the same lock and session timeouts as Engine.Apply, refuses a dirty database or a checksum mismatch, and returns ErrNoDown before running anything when any selected version has no down file. A transactional down runs in one transaction together with the history update; the row becomes rolled_back, so the version is pending again and the next apply runs it anew. A down with -- momo:no-transaction runs statement by statement and, if one fails, leaves the row failed (dirty, settle it with resolve). A rollback undoes schema, not data: write the down so that it can run on a populated table (TestRollbackGroup, TestRollbackNoDown).
  • momo migrate rebase (Engine.Rebase(ctx, target, desired, name)) takes the directory of the target branch (from git, Momo has no git dependency). It lists every file of the branch's migrations that the target lacks, refuses with the file name when one has no -- momo:generated header, and regenerates one migration on top of the target's latest snapshot. It first validates the target (momo.sum, chain, snapshots) and refuses a broken one, and it refuses a branch migration that has a hand-written .down.sql, naming the file. It writes nothing: the caller deletes the returned files and writes the new ones, which the command does (TestMigrateRebase).

There is no --force-unlock: the PostgreSQL lock is a session advisory lock that the server frees when its holder's connection ends (section 3). --lock-wait exists on apply only. --lock-wait 0s fails immediately when locked. resolve and baseline wait the default 30 s.

Database URL: --url, else the variable named in migrate.url_env.postgres, else MOMO_DATABASE_URL. Prefer the environment, or --url -, which reads the URL from standard input (printf '%s' "$URL" | momo migrate apply --url -): a --url value shows in the process list of a shared host, and momo prints a warning on stderr when it sees one.

momo.yaml migrate: keys: dir, url_env (maps keyed by dialect), schemas, lock_timeout, statement_timeout (Go durations), exclude, external_extensions (section 7).

docs.title: 3. Apply semantics on PostgreSQL
docs.text: One connection is pinned for the whole run. Order: lock, set timeouts, history table, migrations, reset timeouts, unlock (reset runs first so a small statement_timeout cannot cancel the unlock). Cleanup runs on a context detached from Ctrl-C and has two steps: the two RESETs share one 5 s bound, and the unlock has its own.

docs.title: Lock
docs.text:
pg_try_advisory_lock(id) on the pinned session, polled every 200 ms until --lock-wait (default 30 s) passes. id = FNV-64a of momo:<schema>.momo_migrations, where <schema> is the schema of the resolved history table (the current schema when none exists yet), so schemas are independent. On timeout apply exits 3 with migration lock is held by another process: held by pid=N application_name=X (TestApplyLockWaitTimesOutWithHolder; waiting callers proceed once it is released, TestApplyWaitsForLockRelease).

The lock is session-scoped: it is released when the holder's connection ends, so a crashed process frees it. There is no lock row to delete and no flag to force the lock (--force-unlock was removed: it never did anything). If a lock appears stuck, find the session (pg_stat_activity by the pid in the message) and terminate it with pg_terminate_backend.

apply, resolve and baseline take the lock. plan, status, drift, validate do not.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
• Default: one transaction per migration file, not per batch. The running history row, all statements and the update to applied commit together. A second migration failing never undoes a first that committed.
  • Marked -- momo:no-transaction: the whole file runs with no transaction, one autocommitted statement at a time, with statements_applied updated after each. Every statement in that file loses atomicity, not only the concurrent one. Only the directive selects this mode on apply; apply does not inspect statements. diff writes the directive when it renders a concurrent index. A hand-written file must carry the directive itself: otherwise PostgreSQL rejects CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside a transaction, the version is recorded rolled_back, and it can be retried after you add the directive. diff never mixes the two modes in one file: when a diff holds both transactional DDL and statements that must run outside a transaction, it writes two migrations, the transactional one first and a trailing <name>_no_tx one that carries the directive (one second later version). A failure in the first file rolls it back whole. A diff with only such statements writes the single no-transaction file.
  • Statements run one by one with no bind parameters. The splitter respects strings, comments and $$ bodies; -- momo:split disables dollar-quote awareness and splits at every semicolon.

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY applies correctly when it is in a no-transaction file: the index is valid and the version is applied (TestCreateIndexConcurrentlyApply). diff produces it from Concurrently() on a model index, and for ADD UNIQUE and the VALIDATE CONSTRAINT of an ADD CHECK (section 5).

docs.title: Session timeouts
docs.text:
Applied with SET on the pinned session, RESET at the end:

Setting momo.yaml Default Notes lock_timeout migrate.lock_timeout 5 s A DDL statement that cannot get its table lock within the limit fails with SQLSTATE 55P03; the transaction rolls back and the version stays retryable. Key absent: 5 s. 0s sets lock_timeout = 0, which disables the limit. statement_timeout migrate.statement_timeout not set Left as the role or server default. A role-level statement_timeout therefore applies to long migrations such as index builds. Use a migration role without it. Key absent: untouched. 0s sends SET statement_timeout = 0, which disables the limit even when the role has one (for a long index build).

If RESET fails, the connection is discarded rather than returned to the pool.

docs.title: PgBouncer and other poolers
docs.text: Run migrations on a direct connection or a session-pooled one. Under transaction pooling the advisory lock, the SET lock_timeout and the search_path belong to a server connection that the next statement may not reuse, so the lock does not protect and the timeouts can leak or not apply. The driver's default query mode is PgBouncer-safe for application queries; the migration engine through PgBouncer is not tested in v0.6.0. A startup search_path is also not reliable through a pooler, so set the schema on the role or on a direct connection.

docs.title: 3a. SQLite
docs.text:
migrate/sqlite is the SQLite migration dialect. It is a library API: pass it to the engine with migrate.WithDialect(sqlite.New()) and a driver/sqlitedriver driver (cgo, not Windows). The momo migrate command does not select it yet, so there is no --dialect sqlite. The tests that pin the behavior below run on a real SQLite in the integration suite (TestSQLiteInspectRoundTrip, TestSQLiteAlterDecision, TestSQLiteRebuild, TestSQLiteLockTable, TestSQLiteEngineLifecycle, TestSQLiteRenderApplyInspectDiffIsZero).

Inspection. Tables, columns (type, NOT NULL, default, collation, generated expression), the primary key, UNIQUE constraints, indexes (including expression and partial indexes), foreign keys, CHECK constraints, views and triggers. The momo_migrations and momo_migration_lock tables, the sqlite_ tables, virtual tables and the shadow tables of virtual tables are left out. An INTEGER PRIMARY KEY of a rowid table is reported with identity by_default, and the schema normalizer gives that column the same identity on the model side, so the two compare equal. A trigger is its CREATE TRIGGER text (schema.Trigger.Definition), compared after whitespace and case outside quotes are normalized. Extensions, native enums, functions, policies, partitions, row-level security and schemas do not exist on SQLite and are never reported.

Enums. SQLite has no enum type. A TEXT column that carries CHECK ("col" IN ('a', 'b')) is inspected as an enum column whose enum is named <table>_<column>, and Engine.Diff writes an enum column back as that CHECK. A model enum therefore round-trips without a diff only when it is named <table>_<column>. create_enum and drop_enum produce no statement; alter_enum_add_value rebuilds the tables that use the enum.

ALTER or rebuild. SQLite changes a table in place only for these: ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO, RENAME COLUMN, ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, and index, view and trigger statements. The renderer uses them when the restrictions in the SQLite documentation allow it: an added column must not be PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, a stored generated column, an enum or identity column, or NOT NULL without a non-NULL default, and its default must not be CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (or CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_TIME) or a parenthesised expression; a dropped column must not be in the primary key, a UNIQUE constraint, an index (key or WHERE), a CHECK, a foreign key (either side), a generated column's expression, a trigger or a view. Everything else (alter_column, any primary key, unique, check or foreign key change, and an add or drop of a column that breaks a restriction) rebuilds the table, and all changes to that table in the same diff become one rebuild.

The rebuild follows the 12 steps in the SQLite documentation. diff writes them as plain statements into the up file and puts -- momo:sqlite-foreign-keys-off at the top of the file. On apply the engine runs PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF outside the transaction (the pragma does nothing inside one), runs the file in one transaction and turns enforcement back on afterwards, also when the migration failed. The statements are: drop every view and trigger that mentions the table (directly or through another view), CREATE TABLE "new_<table>", INSERT ... SELECT of the columns the old and new table share, DROP TABLE, RENAME, CREATE INDEX for each index, recreate the dropped views and triggers that the desired schema keeps unchanged, and PRAGMA foreign_key_check. If that pragma returns a row the statement fails with momo.ErrForeignKeyViolation naming the table and row, and the transaction rolls back (TestSQLiteRebuildOrphanRollsBack). Row count and content, indexes, triggers and views survive (TestSQLiteRebuild, TestSQLiteRebuildKeepsDataAndObjects) and foreign keys are enforced again afterwards (TestSQLiteRebuildFKStillEnforced).

Limits of the rebuild:

  • After each recreated view the file runs SELECT 1 FROM "view" LIMIT 0, because CREATE VIEW does not check the names in its query. A view that names a dropped column therefore fails the migration. sqlite.Rebuild with migrate.RunStatements reports that as migrate.ErrRebuildBlocked naming the view; a migration read back from a file has lost the statement hints, so the engine reports the failing statement number instead.
  • A trigger body is resolved only when the trigger fires, so a trigger that names a dropped column is recreated and fails later.
  • A table can be rebuilt only if it has columns in common with the new definition; INSERT is skipped otherwise.
  • sqlite.Rebuild and sqlite.Capture rebuild from a live connection (captured views and triggers are recreated verbatim); the engine path rebuilds from the snapshot instead.
  • A model cannot declare WITHOUT ROWID, STRICT or AUTOINCREMENT, so a table that has one in the database and not in the model is not a difference: diff and AutoMigrate leave it alone and a rebuild writes it back (TestSQLiteAutoMigrateWithStrictTable). Asking for one the table lacks is refused by diff (write a custom migration). schema.Table carries Strict and Autoincrement; inspection reads them. A rebuild of an AUTOINCREMENT table copies its sqlite_sequence value to the new table, so ids of deleted rows are not handed out again (TestSQLiteStrictAutoincrementRoundTrip). An INTEGER PRIMARY KEY DESC is not a rowid alias and is not reported as an identity.
  • A down migration that rebuilds a table carries the same -- momo:sqlite-foreign-keys-off line; Rollback honours it as apply does (TestSQLiteRollbackRebuildKeepsChildRows).

Unsupported. These fail with an error that wraps momo.ErrUnsupported instead of being dropped: create_schema, create_extension, the policy and row-level-security changes, the function changes, materialized views, views with indexes, index storage parameters, an access method other than b-tree, operator classes, NULLS FIRST/LAST in an index, column comments, serial identity, identity on anything but an INTEGER primary key, partitioning.
