docs.title: Rewrite recipe
docs.text:
1. Commit your work first, because the next steps edit files in place, then fetch the release: go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@v0.4.0.
  2. Save the raw markdown of this page (not the rendered HTML) as upgrading.md in your module root and run the block below from there. It turns the table into gofmt -r rules and applies them to the Go files that import github.com/azrtydxb/momo by that exact path, skipping vendor/. It rewrites the rows of plain identifiers (functions, types and constants), stops with an error when it finds no file or generates no rule, and does not touch a file that imports momo under an alias or with a dot import; the compiler lists what is left there.
files=$(grep -rl --include='*.go' 'github.com/azrtydxb/momo"' . | grep -v /vendor/)
rules=$(awk -F'`' 'NF == 7 && $1 ~ /^\| *$/ && $2 ~ /^momo\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/ { printf "gofmt -r \"%s -> %s\" -w \"$@\"\n", $2, $6 }' upgrading.md)
[ -n "$files" ] || { echo "no Go file imports momo" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "$rules" ] || { echo "no rules: upgrading.md must be the raw markdown of this page" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "$rules" | sh -s -- $files
  1. Rewrite the momo.Tx.* and momo.DB.* rows by hand, because the receiver moves into the argument list: recv.Old(ctx, args) becomes pkg.New(ctx, recv, args). A DB advisory call must pass a transaction (see the paragraph on the advisory locks below). The Validate method of the old SearchSettings type is a plain rename: step 2 rewrites the type, and Validate stays a method of vecsearch.Settings.
  2. In every file, import each new package that now appears in it (arrayop., fts., ...) by the full path in the second column of the table, then build. The compiler lists whatever is left.

A row never changes the SQL a query produces; only the Go name and import path change.

One type gained methods: sqlfn.CurrentSchemaExpr now has the comparison and ordering methods (Eq, In, Asc, ...) the other function results have, so sqlfn.CurrentSchema().Eq("app") compiles, where the old root function's result had no such method.

The advisory lock methods became functions: tx.AdvisoryXactLock(ctx, 42) is now advisory.XactLock(ctx, tx, 42), and the same for advisory.XactLockString and the Try forms. The transaction is the second argument and its type is *momo.Tx. The DB methods always returned momo.ErrValidation, because a transaction-scoped lock outside a transaction is released at once; the functions turn that into a compile error, so a caller that used the DB form must open a transaction with db.Tx or db.Begin. A dialect other than PostgreSQL still fails with momo.ErrUnsupported.

docs.title: What did not move
docs.text:
These stay in momo, with the reason:

  • Func and FuncExpr: the generic SQL function escape hatch, which the new packages build on.
  • Coalesce, Value, SQL and TypedSQL: bound-value and raw-fragment building blocks of the expression core. sqlfn.CoalesceExpr takes expression arguments instead.
  • The vector column types (VectorColumn and its variants): generated code references them.
  • The hook interfaces (Hook, QueryEvent, RelationHook, RelationEvent): DB stores the hooks and calls them.
  • The basic aggregates (Agg[T], CountAll, Sum, Avg, Min, Max): Having and select lists are typed on Agg.
  • Tx.SetLocal: a method of Tx, and other helpers call it.

docs.title: Vector search
docs.text: Momo supports pgvector on PostgreSQL: value types, typed distance expressions, HNSW and IVFFlat index declarations, scoped search settings, plan inspection and an opt-in binary wire codec. It also runs the float32 and bit vector builders on SQLite with sqlite-vec, and the distance builders on MariaDB. This page describes what is built. Every Go snippet below is an Example function in col_example_vector_test.go (package momo_test), vector/example_test.go (package vector_test) or vecsearch/example_test.go (package vecsearch_test), so go test compiles it and checks its printed output.

docs.title: Platforms and versions
docs.text:
• SQLite with sqlite-vec v0.1.6, through driver/sqlitedriver (cgo, not Windows); see SQLite and sqlite-vec below.
  • PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension. Integration tests run against pgvector 0.8.7 (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg17 primary, 0.8.7-pg16 for an older major). The iterative scan settings need pgvector 0.8.0 or newer.
  • The vector extension must be installed by a role that may create it. Momo never installs it at connect time. A missing extension surfaces as momo.ErrUnsupported from a migration, with the extension named in the message. A search settings call checks the installed version the same way.

docs.title: Not available
docs.text:
• Hybrid search on SQLite and MySQL: momo.HybridSearch needs PostgreSQL and returns ErrUnsupported elsewhere; see Hybrid search.
  • MySQL: the server stores vectors but has no distance function, so a distance query fails with ErrUnsupported; see "MariaDB and MySQL" below. The momo migrate command does not run migrate/mysql, which renders its statements as-is, so a MySQL or MariaDB VECTOR column is created by your own DDL.

docs.title: Value types
docs.text:
The vector package holds the four Go types. Each has a Validate(dim) method, a Value method that produces the pgvector text form and a Scan method that reads it back. Validation errors wrap vector.ErrInvalidVector, which the root package re-exports as momo.ErrInvalidVector.

Go type PostgreSQL type Notes vector.Vector vector(n) float32, dimension 1 to 16000 (vector.MaxDim) vector.HalfVector halfvec(n) float32 in Go, float16 in storage, each value within 65504 vector.SparseVector sparsevec(n) Dim, zero-based strictly increasing Indices, vector.SparseVector.Values vector.Bits bit(n) Len bits packed most significant bit first, trailing bits 0

Value rules, enforced before a value reaches the server:

  • The length must equal the column dimension declared on the VectorColumn, unless the column is dimensionless (see Dimensionless columns).
  • NaN and Inf are rejected.
  • A halfvec component must satisfy |x| <= 65504.
  • A dimension above 16000 is rejected for vector and halfvec.
  • A sparsevec has at most 16000 stored elements (vector.MaxSparseNNZ) and a dimension up to 1,000,000,000 (vector.MaxSparseDim). Its text form uses one-based indices, as pgvector does, while Indices is zero-based.
  • A bit string has at most vector.MaxBits bits, the PostgreSQL limit.

The Example functions ExampleVector, ExampleHalfVector, ExampleSparseVector and ExampleBits in vector/example_test.go show the validation and the text forms:

v := vector.Vector{1, 2.5, -3}
fmt.Println(v.Validate(3))      // <nil>
text, _ := v.Value()
fmt.Println(text)               // [1,2.5,-3]
errors.Is(v.Validate(4), vector.ErrInvalidVector) // true

docs.title: Columns and distances
docs.text:
A momo.VectorColumn[V] is a typed column descriptor that carries the declared dimension. Generated code emits one for every field of a vector package type, with the dimension from the dim tag, so document.Embedding passes straight to a distance builder. Build one by hand with momo.NewVectorColumn only for a table the generator does not cover.

A vector column offers the predicates, ordering and write methods of a plain column (Eq, In, IsNull, IsNotNull, IsDistinctFrom, Asc, Desc, Set, SetExpr, SetDefault, SetExcluded), except the range comparisons Lt, Le, Gt, Ge and Between: vectors have no meaningful total order, so use a distance builder to order them. A nullable field (*vector.Vector) gets momo.NullVectorColumn, which adds SetNull.

A vector field tagged read_only, create_only or immutable gets the matching ReadOnlyVectorColumn, CreateOnlyVectorColumn or ImmutableVectorColumn. They keep the write restriction of the plain permission columns (no Set on a read-only column, an insert-only Set on the other two) and every distance builder accepts them, so a read-only embedding can be searched.

The distance builders take a column and a query vector of the same type. The builders live in package github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vecop. Each returns a vecop.Expr, an Expression[float64] that works in the select list, in comparisons and in OrderBy. Asc() orders nearest first and is the default; Desc() orders farthest first.

Builder pgvector operator Column types SQLite function vecop.L2 <-> vector, halfvec, sparse vec_distance_l2 vecop.InnerProduct <#> vector, halfvec, sparse none vecop.Cosine <=> vector, halfvec, sparse vec_distance_cosine vecop.L1 <+> vector, halfvec, sparse vec_distance_l1 vecop.Hamming <~> bit vec_distance_hamming vecop.Jaccard <%> bit none

vecop.InnerProduct is pgvector's <#>, which returns the negative inner product so that ascending order means closest. Passing a dense vector to a bit builder, or the reverse, does not compile (vecop/testdata/compilefail).

The query vector is a bound argument. A dimension mismatch (except on a dimensionless column, see Dimensionless columns), NaN or an out-of-range value is a build error wrapping ErrValidation, reported by SQL() or by the first execution, never a server error. A metric the dialect lacks is a build error wrapping ErrUnsupported. The metrics per dialect come from dialect.Dialect.Vector:

for _, name := range []dialect.Name{dialect.Postgres, dialect.SQLite} {
    caps := dialect.For(name).Vector
    fmt.Println(name, caps.Metrics, caps.Indexes)
}
// postgres [l2 ip cosine l1 hamming jaccard] [hnsw ivfflat]
// sqlite [l2 l1 cosine hamming] []

A nearest-neighbour query (Example_vectorNearest):

c, err := momo.Select[example.Document](db).
    OrderBy(vecop.Cosine(document.Embedding, query).Asc()).
    Limit(5).
    SQL()
// ... ORDER BY ("documents"."embedding" <=> $1) ASC LIMIT $2

Reading the distance next to a column subset needs a projection struct (momo.Projection, From and Columns; see projections). A projection read From a table with a soft-delete column gets the same automatic filter as a model, so soft-deleted rows stay out of the results. Add the predicate yourself only when From is a subquery or a hand-built TableRef.

docs.title: Declaring vector columns and indexes
docs.text:
The generator maps vector.Vector, vector.HalfVector, vector.SparseVector and vector.Bits fields to vector, halfvec, sparsevec and bit columns. The dim tag sets the dimension, and sparsevec and bit require it:

Embedding vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"`

Generation adds CREATE EXTENSION vector to the schema when a vector column or index is present. An ANN index needs an operator class, and pgvector's hnsw has no default one, so declare vector indexes in MomoConfig (the reference model is internal/testmodels/example/models.go):

func (d *Document) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
    c.Index("documents_embedding_hnsw", &d.Embedding).
        Method("hnsw").
        Opclass(&d.Embedding, "vector_cosine_ops").
        With("m", "16").
        With("ef_construction", "64")
}

The generator and schema.ValidateVectorIndex reject an index that pgvector would refuse, before any SQL runs. The error wraps schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex. schema.VectorIndexOpClass(type, metric) returns the opclass for a column type and metric (ExampleValidateVectorIndex).

docs.title: Index limits
docs.text:
Method Types Dimension limit Opclasses (suffix after <type>_) hnsw vector, halfvec, sparsevec, bit vector 2000, halfvec 4000, bit 64000 l2, ip, cosine, l1; bit: hamming, jaccard ivfflat vector, halfvec, bit vector 2000, halfvec 4000, bit 64000 l2, ip, cosine; bit: hamming
  • ivfflat does not support sparsevec.
  • hnsw accepts the storage parameters m (2 to 100, default 16) and ef_construction (4 to 1000, default 64, at least 2*m).
  • ivfflat requires an explicit lists parameter (1 to 32768). Momo does not rely on the server default of 100.
  • An index covers one plain column. Expression parts are rejected.
  • The hnsw and ivfflat methods are pgvector's. schema.ValidateVectorIndex rejects them for another dialect, with an error that wraps schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex. MariaDB has its own VECTOR INDEX; see "MariaDB and MySQL" below.

docs.title: Dimensionless columns
docs.text:
A vector.Vector or vector.HalfVector field without a dim tag maps to the bare vector or halfvec type. Use it for a store whose embedding size depends on the configured model: each row carries its size in a dims column, and every search filters on it.

type KbChunk struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:kb_chunks"`
    ID         int64         `momo:"pk,identity"`
    Dims       int
    Embedding  vector.Vector // no dim: any size
}
  • Generation emits a plain vector column and a momo.VectorColumn whose Dim() is zero. sparsevec and bit still require dim.
  • A distance argument of any size is accepted; it is checked against its own size, so NaN, Inf and an empty vector are still rejected. The column never catches a size mismatch itself.
  • pgvector fails a distance between two sizes, so filter on dims in the same query: Where(chunk.Dims.Eq(len(q))) plus OrderBy(vecop.Cosine(chunk.Embedding, q).Asc()).
  • The migration round-trips the bare type and the next diff is empty.
  • Limit: pgvector cannot build an hnsw or ivfflat index on a dimensionless column. Momo refuses one, with an error that wraps schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex and names the column. Searches run as a sequential scan over the filtered rows. An expression or partial index such as ((embedding::vector(1536))) WHERE dims = 1536 is not supported yet: expression parts are rejected.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
migrate.Diff emits the extension, the table and the index, and migrate/postgres renders them (Example_vectorMigration):

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "vector"
CREATE TABLE "documents" ("id" bigint NOT NULL, "embedding" vector(3) NOT NULL, ...)
CREATE INDEX "documents_embedding_hnsw" ON "documents" USING "hnsw" ("embedding" "vector_cosine_ops") WITH ("m" = 16, "ef_construction" = 64)

Inspection reads method, operator class and storage parameters back, so an unchanged vector index produces no diff. A default operator class (ivfflat on vector, vector_l2_ops) is stored as empty, which matches inspection.

docs.title: Search settings
docs.text:
vecsearch.Settings (package github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vecsearch) applies pgvector settings for one transaction. Zero values leave the server default alone. Settings use set_config(name, value, true), so they revert at commit or rollback and never reach a pooled connection, which makes them safe behind PgBouncer in transaction mode.

Field Setting Range HNSWEfSearch hnsw.ef_search 1 to 1000 HNSWIterativeScan hnsw.iterative_scan vecsearch.IterativeOff, vecsearch.IterativeRelaxedOrder, vecsearch.IterativeStrictOrder HNSWMaxScanTuples hnsw.max_scan_tuples 1 to 2147483647 (server default 20000) HNSWScanMemMultiplier hnsw.scan_mem_multiplier 1 to 1000, float, a multiple of work_mem IVFFlatProbes ivfflat.probes 1 to 32768 IVFFlatIterativeScan ivfflat.iterative_scan vecsearch.IterativeOff or vecsearch.IterativeRelaxedOrder IVFFlatMaxProbes ivfflat.max_probes 1 to 32768 ExactSearch enable_indexscan, enable_bitmapscan set to off bool

vecsearch.Settings.Validate reports a value outside its range as ErrValidation. The iterative fields, HNSWMaxScanTuples, HNSWScanMemMultiplier and IVFFlatMaxProbes need pgvector 0.8.0 or newer. When any of them is set, vecsearch.Apply reads pg_extension and returns ErrUnsupported on an older or missing extension, instead of letting the server accept an unknown setting as a placeholder.

Use vecsearch.With for a block, or vecsearch.Apply inside a transaction you already have (ExampleWith, ExampleApply):

settings := vecsearch.Settings{
    HNSWEfSearch:      100,
    HNSWIterativeScan: vecsearch.IterativeRelaxedOrder, // needs pgvector 0.8
    HNSWMaxScanTuples: 20000,
    HNSWScanMemMultiplier: 2, // pgvector 0.8: iterative scan memory, times work_mem
}
err := vecsearch.With(ctx, db, settings, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
    _, err := momo.Select[example.Document](tx).
        OrderBy(vecop.Cosine(document.Embedding, query).Asc()).
        Limit(10).
        All(ctx)
    return err
})

Tx.SetLocal(ctx, name, value) sets any run-time parameter the same way. Never pass an untrusted name: the name is bound, but set_config can change role or search_path.

docs.title: Exact versus approximate search
docs.text: An index scan is approximate. ExactSearch turns off index and bitmap scans for the rest of the transaction, so a vector ORDER BY scans the table and returns the exact nearest neighbours. The switches are not specific to vector indexes: every other index lookup in that transaction also falls back to a sequential scan, so keep the transaction short and dedicated to the exact query.

docs.title: Filters, iterative scans and result counts
docs.text:
With a selective filter and LIMIT k, pgvector with iterative scan off scans the index once and applies the filter afterwards, so it can return fewer than k rows. TestFilteredANNIterativeScan reproduces this: a filter that matches 1% of 20000 rows returns fewer than 10 rows with iterative scan off, and 10 with relaxed_order and HNSWMaxScanTuples 1,000,000.

relaxed_order keeps scanning until enough rows pass the filter or hnsw.max_scan_tuples is reached. The result is therefore still approximate, and it can be shorter than k when the filter matches fewer rows than that bound allows. strict_order (hnsw only) keeps exact distance order while it scans.

docs.title: Hybrid search
docs.text:
momo.HybridSearch fuses a PostgreSQL full-text leg and a cosine-distance vector leg with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) in one statement. Each leg picks its own best TextCandidates and VectorCandidates rows (default 100, at most 1000), ranks them, and a row scores the sum of 1/(RRFK+rank) over the legs it appears in (RRFK defaults to 60 and must be at least 1). The text leg ranks with ts_rank_cd over websearch_to_tsquery; the vector leg uses <=>. Ties break on the primary key ascending, in each leg's ranking and in the final order, so the result does not depend on insertion order. The vector leg orders by distance alone so an hnsw or ivfflat index can serve it; when rows tie on distance exactly at the candidate cut-off, which of them become candidates is not defined.

hits, err := momo.HybridSearch[Article](db, momo.HybridSpec{
    Text:        articleBody,
    TextConfig:  "english",
    Query:       userInput,
    Vector:      articleEmb,
    QueryVector: queryEmbedding,
    Limit:       10,
}).All(ctx)
// each hit has .Row (the model) and .Score

The model needs a single-column primary key, Query must not be empty (use a plain vector query for that), and HybridSpec.Text and HybridSpec.Vector must be columns of the model's table; otherwise the call returns ErrValidation. Soft-deleted rows are left out. The vector leg takes the dense vector type only (not halfvec, sparsevec or bit) and skips rows with a NULL embedding and rows whose cosine distance is NaN (zero vectors). HybridQuery.SQL returns the statement and its arguments without running it. The vector leg can use an hnsw or ivfflat index on the vector column with vector_cosine_ops. The text leg binds the configuration as a parameter, and a GIN expression index on to_tsvector('english', body) needs a constant configuration in its definition, so PostgreSQL may not match it to a bound regconfig; check the plan with EXPLAIN. Without an index a leg scans the table, so the candidate counts bound the work after the scan, not the scan itself. For a different mix of signals, write your own score as shown in full-text search.

docs.title: Verifying index use
docs.text:
SelectQuery.Explain(ctx) runs EXPLAIN (never EXPLAIN ANALYZE), binds the parameters and returns the plan text. It does not execute the query. Run it inside the transaction whose settings you want to see (ExampleSelectQuery_Explain):

plan, err := momo.Select[example.Document](db).
    OrderBy(vecop.L2(document.Embedding, query).Asc()).
    Limit(10).
    Explain(ctx)
// look for "Index Scan using documents_embedding_hnsw"

TestVectorIndexUsed and TestExactSearchBypassesVectorIndex use this pattern to assert that the index is used, and that ExactSearch stops using it. Expect a sequential scan on a small table, because the planner prefers it below a few thousand rows. Explain returns ErrUnsupported on MySQL and MariaDB.

docs.title: PostgreSQL wire format
docs.text:
By default vector values travel as text. The binary codec is opt-in and lives in driver/pgxdriver:

  • pgxdriver.ConfigureVectors(cfg) installs an AfterConnect hook that looks up the OIDs of vector, halfvec and sparsevec and registers codecs for them and for bit. Call it before pgxpool.NewWithConfig. The lookup runs once per connection: a connection opened before CREATE EXTENSION vector stays on text until the pool recycles it.
  • pgxdriver.WithVectorFormat(pgxdriver.VectorBinary) asks for binary parameters. It needs a describe-based exec mode (WithExecMode with pgx.QueryExecModeDescribeExec, CacheStatement or CacheDescribe); pgx's default QueryExecModeExec always sends text, with identical results.
  • COPY always uses binary and so needs ConfigureVectors.
  • Decoders bound every length they read before they allocate.

ExampleConfigureVectors shows the setup:

cfg, err := pgxpool.ParseConfig("postgres://localhost/app")
pgxdriver.ConfigureVectors(cfg)
pool, err := pgxpool.NewWithConfig(ctx, cfg)
db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool, pgxdriver.WithVectorFormat(pgxdriver.VectorBinary)))

docs.title: Differences between approaches
docs.text:
• pgvector exact search (ExactSearch) reads every row and returns the true nearest neighbours. Index search (hnsw, ivfflat) is approximate and tuned with hnsw.ef_search, ivfflat.probes and the iterative settings.
  • sqlite-vec is brute-force KNN with no ANN index. A request for an ANN index on SQLite is ErrUnsupported. SQLite supports float32 vectors (l2, l1, cosine) and bit vectors (hamming) only; halfvec and sparsevec arguments, inner product and Jaccard return ErrUnsupported at build time. SQLite bit vectors keep only the packed bytes, so the declared column length is authoritative for Len. See SQLite and sqlite-vec.
  • vecsearch.Apply on SQLite: ExactSearch alone is a no-op, every search is already exact, and any other field is ErrUnsupported. On MySQL and MariaDB every non-zero setting, ExactSearch included, is ErrUnsupported, because Tx.SetLocal has no transaction-scoped setting there.
  • MariaDB VECTOR INDEX is approximate; see "MariaDB and MySQL" below.

docs.title: SQLite and sqlite-vec
docs.text:
driver/sqlitedriver links sqlite-vec v0.1.6 (the version vec_version() reports; sqlitedriver.SQLiteVecVersion is the release it is tested with, and Open fails with ErrUnsupported on another minor or major version but accepts a later patch release of the same minor). The same typed builders that serve pgvector render sqlite-vec's scalar functions, and the integration tests run them against a real SQLite database: col_vector_sqlite_integration_test.go in the root package and TestSQLiteVectorParity in driver/sqlitedriver. It needs cgo and does not build on Windows. The SQLite migration dialect (migrate/sqlite) is library only, and the generator refuses vector fields on SQLite, so you create the table with your own DDL.

Columns. A vector is a plain BLOB column; sqlite-vec has no declared dimension, so the length is guarded by a CHECK. momo.SQLiteVectorType and momo.SQLiteBitsType return the definition to put after the column name: BLOB CHECK (length("emb") = 12) for three float32 elements and BLOB CHECK (length("bits") = 1) for eight bits. A vector of the wrong size is then refused by the database as ErrCheckViolation. A dimensionless column is ErrUnsupported, because there is no length to check.

Values. vector.Vector is stored as a little-endian float32 blob and read back from one, and vector.Bits as its packed bytes (most significant bit first, as in pgvector: bit 0 is the top bit of byte 0). Both are validated before they are bound (NaN, Inf, an empty vector, a bad bit length are ErrInvalidVector), because a blob has no text form that would reject them later. A *vector.Vector or *vector.Bits field is nullable: nil binds NULL. vector.HalfVector and vector.SparseVector have no sqlite-vec type, so binding one, or searching with one, is ErrUnsupported when the query is built. A bit vector read from SQLite has a Len of 8 times its byte count, so the column length is the authority for a length that is not a multiple of 8.

Metrics. These are exactly the functions v0.1.6 registers:

Builder SQLite function Column type vecop.L2 vec_distance_l2 vector.Vector vecop.L1 vec_distance_l1 vector.Vector vecop.Cosine vec_distance_cosine vector.Vector vecop.Hamming vec_distance_hamming(vec_bit(column), vec_bit(argument)) vector.Bits vecop.InnerProduct none: ErrUnsupported at build time vecop.Jaccard none: ErrUnsupported at build time

The query vector is a bound argument. When the column is sensitive, it shows as momo.RedactedArg in hook events, on a query and on an insert, while the database gets the real blob. Distances work in the select list, in a comparison and in OrderBy (Asc nearest first, Desc farthest first). Results are held to the plain-Go reference in internal/vectorparity: the top-10 ids of cosine, L2 and L1 search over 300 vectors equal the reference exactly. The reference is the one pgvector exact search and MariaDB are held to for cosine, and when a PostgreSQL URL is set TestSQLiteVectorParity also loads the same vectors into pgvector and requires the same ids for cosine, L2 and L1.

Indexes. sqlite-vec compares every row, so it has no approximate index and dialect.For(dialect.SQLite).Vector.Indexes is empty, and schema.ValidateVectorIndex rejects an index for SQLite with schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex. An internal check turns a request for any index method on a dialect that lists none into ErrUnsupported; it becomes public when a SQLite migration dialect needs it. SQLite itself does not parse an index method, so nothing is accepted silently. ExactSearch in vecsearch.Settings is a no-op (every search is exact) and any other setting is ErrUnsupported. The sqlite-vec virtual tables (vec0, which have an index of their own) are not wrapped.

Bring up a throwaway database for your own tests with momotest/sqlitetest.

docs.title: MariaDB and MySQL
docs.text:
MariaDB 11.8 supports float32 vectors through mysqldriver. MySQL 9.x stores them but cannot compare them.

Capability MariaDB 11.8 MySQL 9.7 MySQL 8.4 Column type VECTOR(N) VECTOR(N) none: ErrUnsupported vector.Vector write and read yes yes no vecop.L2 VEC_DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN(col, VEC_FromText(?)) ErrUnsupported ErrUnsupported vecop.Cosine VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(col, VEC_FromText(?)) ErrUnsupported ErrUnsupported Other metrics, other types ErrUnsupported (inner product, L1, halfvec, sparsevec, bit) ErrUnsupported ErrUnsupported ANN index VECTOR INDEX, approximate none none Capabilities().Vectors true false false

MySQL Community has no distance function (the distance functions belong to HeatWave), so a distance query on MySQL fails at build time with ErrUnsupported. Momo never falls back to a scan or to a Go-side sort.

A vector.Vector bound on MySQL or MariaDB travels as its text form wrapped in VEC_FromText (MariaDB) or STRING_TO_VECTOR (MySQL), on every typed bind path: insert, update, equality and distance. Stored vectors scan back from the server's binary float32 form. A column marked sensitive masks the vector in hook events exactly as on PostgreSQL.

A MariaDB VECTOR INDEX needs a NOT NULL vector(N) column and accepts M from 3 to 200 and DISTANCE of euclidean or cosine. It serves only the metric it was built with, and an ORDER BY distance with LIMIT uses it. To get the exact nearest neighbours from the same table, add + 0 to the distance in a raw query, which keeps the server from using the index. schema.ValidateMariaDBVectorIndex checks a declaration and schema.MariaDBVectorIndexClause renders it. momo.MySQLVectorType gives the column type for a server version and refuses MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB before 11.7 with a diagnostic that names the version.

docs.title: Coming from Bun
docs.text:
This page maps the Bun calls you use every day to their Momo equivalents. Bun and Momo are both close to SQL, so most calls translate one to one. The differences are in what Momo does not do for you: it writes exactly the SQL of the call you made, never retries, and never saves more than the model you pass. To convert existing Bun structs automatically, read importing models from other ORMs (momo import bun).

The programs on this page are compiled against the models of the quickstart example: an Author that has many Post rows. Blocks fenced as go notest show code that is not compiled here.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Bun Momo bun:"table:users,alias:u" on BaseModel momo:"table:users" on the embedded momo.Model bun:",pk,autoincrement" momo:"pk,identity" bun:",notnull,unique" momo:"notnull,unique" bun:",nullzero" a pointer field (Momo writes the zero value otherwise) bun:"rel:has-many,join:id=author_id" momo:"has_many,fk:AuthorID" bun:"rel:belongs-to,join:author_id=id" momo:"belongs_to,fk:AuthorID" NewSelect().Model(&rows).Where(...) momo.Select[T] with Where and All NewInsert().Model(&row).Exec(ctx) momo.Insert[T] with Model and Exec NewUpdate().Model(&row).WherePK() momo.Update[T] with Set, Where and Exec NewDelete().Model(&row).WherePK() momo.Delete[T] with Where and Exec .Relation("Posts") .Preload(author.Posts) on the select, or momo.Load db.RunInTx(ctx, nil, func(ctx, tx bun.Tx)) db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {...}) bun migrate.NewMigrator(db, migrations) momo migrate diff <name>, then momo migrate apply errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) errors.Is(err, momo.ErrNotFound)

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Bun reads its struct tags at run time through reflection. Momo reads the momo: tags and the optional MomoConfig method statically, when you run momo generate; the generator writes typed column handles such as author.Name.

``go notest type Author struct { momo.Modelmomo:"table:authors"ID int64momo:"pk,identity"Name stringmomo:"size:200,notnull,unique"`

Posts []Post `momo:"has_many,fk:AuthorID"`

} `` One behaviour differs from Bun and matters when you port a model:nullzeromakes Bun write NULL for a zero value. Momo writes the zero value you gave it; use a pointer field to write NULL.momo import bunreports eachnullzerofield aszero-value-handlingand eachdefault:` as a database default.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
A query is built from typed columns, so a misspelled column or a value of the wrong type fails to compile. All returns every row, One returns exactly one row and fails with momo.ErrNotFound when there is none. go package main import ( "context" "fmt" "log" "os" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models/post" ) // recentPosts is the Momo form of NewSelect().Model(&posts).Where("author_id = ?", id).Order("title").Limit(10). func recentPosts(ctx context.Context, q momo.Querier, authorID int64) ([]models.Post, error) { return momo.Select[models.Post](q). Where(post.AuthorID.Eq(authorID)). OrderBy(post.Title.Asc()). Limit(10). All(ctx) } func main() { ctx := context.Background() pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } defer pool.Close() db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool)) posts, err := recentPosts(ctx, db, 1) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } fmt.Println(len(posts), "posts") }

Raw SQL stays available through momo.Exec and momo.Scalars; ? binds the next argument, as in Bun, so a value never becomes part of the SQL text.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
Bun's .Relation("Posts") joins or runs a second query depending on the relation. Momo always says which: momo.Load fills a relation on models you already have with one extra query, and SelectQuery.Preload attaches the loader to the query so All, One and First run it for you. A relation is never saved with its parent; write the children with their own insert.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models/author"
)

// authorsWithPosts is NewSelect().Model(&authors).Relation("Posts") in Bun.
func authorsWithPosts(ctx context.Context, q momo.Querier) ([]models.Author, error) {
    return momo.Select[models.Author](q).Preload(author.Posts).All(ctx)
}

// loadPosts fills Posts on authors you already have.
func loadPosts(ctx context.Context, q momo.Querier, authors []models.Author) error {
    return momo.Load(ctx, q, authors, author.Posts)
}

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer pool.Close()
    db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))

    authors, err := authorsWithPosts(ctx, db)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := loadPosts(ctx, db, authors); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Println(len(authors), "authors")
}

See relations for filtering a loaded relation, joins and writing related rows.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Bun has model hooks such as BeforeAppendModel and query hooks added with AddQueryHook. Momo separates the two. Model hooks are typed functions on the model's metadata, HookSet: BeforeInsert, BeforeUpdate, BeforeDelete and AfterLoad, set once at start-up on the Meta value. Observing every statement is momo.WithHook, and per-handle rules such as a tenant filter are interceptors.

```go notest var authorMeta = momo.Meta[Author]{ /* generated metadata */ Hooks: momo.HookSet[Author]{ BeforeInsert: func(ctx context.Context, a *Author) error { a.Name = strings.TrimSpace(a.Name) return nil }, }} 

A model hook runs only on the typed execution methods (`Exec`, `All`, `One` and
so on), not on raw SQL, and an error from a Before hook stops the statement
before any SQL runs.

## Transactions

`RunInTx` in Bun and `db.Tx` in Momo both commit when the function returns nil
and roll back on an error or a panic. Momo calls the function exactly once:
there is no automatic retry, so retry a serialization failure in your own code.
Use the `tx` handle for every statement inside the function.

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "errors"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models/author"
)

func rename(ctx context.Context, db *momo.DB, id int64, name string) error {
    return db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
        a, err := momo.Select[models.Author](tx).Where(author.ID.Eq(id)).One(ctx)
        if errors.Is(err, momo.ErrNotFound) {
            return fmt.Errorf("author %d does not exist", id)
        }
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        _, err = momo.Update[models.Author](tx).
            Set(author.Name.Set(name)).
            Where(author.ID.Eq(a.ID)).
            Exec(ctx)
        return err
    })
}

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer pool.Close()
    db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))

    if err := rename(ctx, db, 1, "Ada Lovelace"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
Bun's migrator runs SQL files or Go functions registered in your program and records them in bun_migrations. Momo's migrations are SQL files that momo migrate diff writes from your models, each with a schema snapshot and a momo.sum checksum file:

momo migrate diff add_authors   # writes <version>_add_authors.up.sql, a snapshot and momo.sum
momo migrate apply              # applies pending files under a lock and records them
momo migrate status

A database that Bun already migrated keeps its schema. Import the SQL migrations and the bun_migrations rows with the Bun history reader (importer/history/bun, see importing) so none of them runs again. Bun migrations written as Go functions cannot be imported; the reader lists them and refuses the import until you convert them to SQL.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Bun returns the driver's error, and sql.ErrNoRows from Scan on an empty result. Momo classifies database errors into sentinels you compare with errors.Is, never with the error text: momo.ErrNotFound for a single-row call that found nothing, momo.ErrUniqueViolation and momo.ErrForeignKeyViolation for constraint failures. All returns an empty slice, not an error, when nothing matches.

docs.title: Coming from Ent
docs.text:
This page maps the Ent calls you use every day to their Momo equivalents. Ent generates a client from schema code; Momo generates typed column handles from plain structs. The differences are in what Momo does not do for you: it writes exactly the SQL of the call you made, never retries, and never saves an edge you did not write. To convert an existing Ent schema automatically, run momo import ent (see importing models from other ORMs): it reads the schema package with go/parser and never compiles or runs it.

The programs on this page are compiled against the models of the quickstart example: an Author that has many Post rows. Blocks fenced as go notest show code that is not compiled here.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: Ent Momo field.String("name").NotEmpty().Unique() Name string with momo:"notnull,unique" field.String("bio").Optional().Nillable() Bio *string field.Int64("id") (the implicit key) ID int64 with momo:"pk,identity" edge.To("posts", Post.Type) Posts []Post with momo:"has_many,fk:AuthorID" edge.From("author", Author.Type).Ref("posts") Author *Author with momo:"belongs_to,fk:AuthorID" client.Author.Query().Where(author.NameEQ(n)) momo.Select[T](db).Where(col.Eq(n)).All(ctx) client.Author.Create().SetName(n).Save(ctx) momo.Insert[T](db).Model(&row).Exec(ctx) client.Author.UpdateOneID(id).SetName(n) momo.Update[T](db).Set(col.Set(n)).Where(...).Exec(ctx) client.Author.DeleteOneID(id).Exec(ctx) momo.Delete[T](db).Where(...).Exec(ctx) .WithPosts() (eager loading) .Preload(author.Posts) on the select, or momo.Load client.Tx(ctx), tx.Commit(), tx.Rollback() db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {...}) client.Schema.Create(ctx) momo migrate diff <name>, then momo migrate apply ent.IsNotFound(err) errors.Is(err, momo.ErrNotFound)

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Ent describes a table with builder chains in a Fields method, and generates a client and a package of predicates per entity. Momo describes a table as a struct and generates typed column handles such as author.Name, which are the predicates and setters you use in queries.

``go notest type Author struct { momo.Modelmomo:"table:authors"ID int64momo:"pk,identity"Name stringmomo:"size:200,notnull,unique"`

Posts []Post `momo:"has_many,fk:AuthorID"`

} ``momo import entconverts the fields, edges, indexes, mixins and theentsql.Annotationtable name it can read as literals. Anything it cannot read without running your code (a many-to-many edge, JSON and UUID fields, a custom key, an unknown builder method) is anunsupportedchange at itsfile:line:col: nothing is written until you remove or convert it. Two behaviours differ from Ent and are reported as changes: - Ent applies a field'sDefaultin Go when the setter was not called. Momo writes the zero value you gave it (zero-value-handling); keep the database default with adefault:tag or a pointer field. - Ent saves an edge only when its setter was called, and Momo saves a relation only when you write it, soedge.Fromwith.Refis reported asimplicit-save` to make you check the write paths.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
A query is built from typed columns, so a misspelled column or a value of the wrong type fails to compile. All returns every row, One returns exactly one row and fails with momo.ErrNotFound when there is none. go package main import ( "context" "fmt" "log" "os" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models" "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models/post" ) // recentPosts is client.Post.Query().Where(post.AuthorID(id)).Order(ent.Asc("title")).Limit(10).All(ctx) in Ent. func recentPosts(ctx context.Context, q momo.Querier, authorID int64) ([]models.Post, error) { return momo.Select[models.Post](q). Where(post.AuthorID.Eq(authorID)). OrderBy(post.Title.Asc()). Limit(10). All(ctx) } func main() { ctx := context.Background() pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } defer pool.Close() db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool)) posts, err := recentPosts(ctx, db, 1) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } fmt.Println(len(posts), "posts") }

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
Ent loads an edge when you ask with WithPosts(), one extra query per edge. Momo does the same and you pick where it happens: momo.Load fills a relation on models you already have, and SelectQuery.Preload attaches the loader to the query so All, One and First run it for you. A relation is never saved with its parent; write the children with their own insert.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models/author"
)

// authorsWithPosts is client.Author.Query().WithPosts().All(ctx) in Ent.
func authorsWithPosts(ctx context.Context, q momo.Querier) ([]models.Author, error) {
    return momo.Select[models.Author](q).Preload(author.Posts).All(ctx)
}

// loadPosts fills Posts on authors you already have.
func loadPosts(ctx context.Context, q momo.Querier, authors []models.Author) error {
    return momo.Load(ctx, q, authors, author.Posts)
}

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer pool.Close()
    db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))

    authors, err := authorsWithPosts(ctx, db)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := loadPosts(ctx, db, authors); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Println(len(authors), "authors")

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Ent hooks wrap mutations (ent.Hook, added with client.Use or in the schema's Hooks method) and see the mutation, not the model. Momo's model hooks are typed functions on the model's metadata, HookSet: BeforeInsert, BeforeUpdate, BeforeDelete and AfterLoad, set once at start-up on the Meta value. They receive the model pointer and may change its values. Observing every statement is momo.WithHook, and per-handle rules such as a tenant filter are interceptors.

```go notest var authorMeta = momo.Meta[Author]{ /* generated metadata */ Hooks: momo.HookSet[Author]{ BeforeInsert: func(ctx context.Context, a *Author) error { a.Name = strings.TrimSpace(a.Name) return nil }, }} 

A model hook runs only on the typed execution methods (`Exec`, `All`, `One` and
so on), not on raw SQL, and an error from a Before hook stops the statement
before any SQL runs. Ent validators, immutable fields and privacy policies are
reported by the importer as `go-side-rule` changes: Momo does not run them.

## Transactions

`client.Tx` in Ent hands you a transactional client that you commit or roll back
yourself. `db.Tx` in Momo takes a function instead: it commits when the function
returns nil and rolls back on an error or a panic. Momo calls the function
exactly once: there is no automatic retry, so retry a serialization failure in
your own code. Use the `tx` handle for every statement inside the function.

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "errors"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models"
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/examples/quickstart/models/author"
)

func rename(ctx context.Context, db *momo.DB, id int64, name string) error {
    return db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
        a, err := momo.Select[models.Author](tx).Where(author.ID.Eq(id)).One(ctx)
        if errors.Is(err, momo.ErrNotFound) {
            return fmt.Errorf("author %d does not exist", id)
        }
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        _, err = momo.Update[models.Author](tx).
            Set(author.Name.Set(name)).
            Where(author.ID.Eq(a.ID)).
            Exec(ctx)
        return err
    })
}

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer pool.Close()
    db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))

    if err := rename(ctx, db, 1, "Ada Lovelace"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
client.Schema.Create applies the schema to the database on the spot, and Ent can also write versioned migration files through Atlas. Momo's migrations are SQL files that momo migrate diff writes from your models, each with a schema snapshot and a momo.sum checksum file:

momo migrate diff add_authors   # writes <version>_add_authors.up.sql, a snapshot and momo.sum
momo migrate apply              # applies pending files under a lock and records them
momo migrate status

If you used Ent's Atlas versioned migrations, the Atlas directory reader (importer/history/atlas, see importing) verifies atlas.sum and converts the history so nothing runs twice. A database created with client.Schema.Create has no history file; run momo migrate baseline on it (see migrations).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Ent returns errors you test with ent.IsNotFound, ent.IsConstraintError and related helpers. Momo classifies database errors into sentinels you compare with errors.Is, never with the error text: momo.ErrNotFound for a single-row call that found nothing, momo.ErrUniqueViolation and momo.ErrForeignKeyViolation for constraint failures. All returns an empty slice, not an error, when nothing matches.

docs.title: Coming from GORM
docs.text:
This page maps the GORM calls you use every day to their Momo equivalents. It does not try to hide the differences: Momo writes exactly the SQL of the call you made, never retries, and never saves more than the model you pass. To convert existing GORM structs automatically, read importing models from other ORMs (momo import gorm).

The programs on this page are compiled against the models of the quickstart example: an Author that has many Post rows. Blocks fenced as go notest show code that is not compiled here.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: GORM Momo gorm:"primaryKey" momo:"pk"; add identity for a generated key gorm:"size:200;not null;uniqueIndex" momo:"size:200,notnull,unique" gorm:"column:author_id;index" momo:"column:author_id,index" db.Where("name = ?", n).Find(&rows) momo.Select[T](db).Where(col.Eq(n)).All(ctx) db.First(&row, id) momo.Select[T](db).Where(col.Eq(id)).One(ctx) db.Create(&row) momo.Insert[T](db).Model(&row).Exec(ctx) db.Model(&row).Update("name", n) momo.Update[T](db).Set(col.Set(n)).Where(...).Exec(ctx) db.Delete(&row) momo.Delete[T](db).Where(...).Exec(ctx) db.Preload("Posts").Find(&rows) momo.Select[T](db).Preload(author.Posts).All(ctx), or momo.Load db.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB)...) db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {...}) db.AutoMigrate(&T{}) momo migrate diff <name>, then momo migrate apply errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) errors.Is(err, momo.ErrNotFound)

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
GORM reads struct tags at run time. Momo reads the momo: tags and the optional MomoConfig method statically, when you run momo generate; the generator writes typed column handles such as author.Name. A Momo struct embeds momo.Model, which carries the table name:

``go notest type Author struct { momo.Modelmomo:"table:authors"ID int64momo:"pk,identity"Name stringmomo:"size:200,notnull,unique"`

Posts []Post `momo:"has_many,fk:AuthorID"`

} `` Three behaviours differ from GORM and matter when you port a model: - GORM replaces a zero value with the column default on insert. Momo writes the zero value you gave it. Use a pointer field to write NULL or to leave a value to the database default. - GORM treats a field namedIDas the key andCreatedAtandUpdatedAtas managed timestamps by convention. Momo uses the tags you wrote. -gorm.DeletedAtsoft delete becomes an explicit soft-delete field; see the [type mapping](https://github.com/azrtydxb/momo/blob/main/TYPE_MAPPING.md).momo import gormreports each of these as a change (zero-value-handling,renamed-type`) with the position of the field.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
GORM calls BeforeCreate, BeforeUpdate, BeforeDelete and AfterFind methods on the model. Momo has the same four points as typed functions on the model's metadata, HookSet: BeforeInsert, BeforeUpdate, BeforeDelete and AfterLoad. They are set once at start-up on the Meta value, not as methods on the struct:

```go notest var authorMeta = momo.Meta[Author]{ /* generated metadata */ Hooks: momo.HookSet[Author]{ BeforeInsert: func(ctx context.Context, a *Author) error { a.Name = strings.TrimSpace(a.Name) return nil }, }} 

A hook runs only on the typed execution methods (`Exec`, `All`, `One` and so
on), not on raw SQL, and an error from a Before hook stops the statement before
any SQL runs. Hooks do not run for relations loaded with `Load` or `Preload`.
Per-handle rules such as a tenant filter belong in an
[interceptor](https://github.com/azrtydxb/momo/blob/main/PRIVACY_RULES.md), which runs before the hooks.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
AutoMigrate compares your structs with the live database and changes it on the spot. Momo's AutoMigrate Go API also exists, but it only adds (tables, columns, indexes), writes no history and is meant for development and tests. For a real database use versioned files:

momo migrate diff add_authors   # writes <version>_add_authors.up.sql, a snapshot and momo.sum
momo migrate apply              # applies pending files under a lock and records them
momo migrate status

If the database already has a schema from GORM, put it under Momo with momo migrate baseline (see migrations); if you ran GORM inside another tool's migrations, import that history so nothing runs twice.
